confirmed.title: PvP: defender evasion is a flat, uncounterable dodge — DEX never answers it in a duel (live path diverges from the tuned sim)
confirmed.claim: In duels the whole DEX-vs-EVA tier system (Stats.dex_tier / graze_through) is bypassed. `_hit_rival` deliberately resolves against NEUTRAL defenses (e_eva = 0), so no dex/eva interaction happens attacker-side; the strike then crosses the wire and lands on the owner via `p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, ...)` with attacker == null, which takes the attacker-less branch and rolls a bare `randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva)`. The striker's DEX is never consulted on either side — it is not even carried on the wire (pvp_strike ships only `pen`). So a duel evasion stack is an uncounterable ~50-65% dodge, contradicting eva_curve's own contract ("answerable by ~matching dex") and, more concretely, the balance harness the PvP numbers were tuned on: pvp_duel_sim._hit DOES model the tier (miss / graze / cancel). Live behaviour and the simulator disagree.
confirmed.evidence:
player_combat.gd:1898-1899 `	var result := Stats.resolve(base_amt * (1.0 - true_frac), dmg_type,
		crit, crit_dmg, 0.0, dex, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, crit_exempt)`  (e_eva argument is 0.0 -> resolve's dex_tier block is a no-op)
net/net_session.gd:3053 `			p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, false, pen)`  (attacker == null)
player.gd:1120-1125 `	else:
		if randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):
			game.spawn_text(global_position + Vector2(0, -40), "DODGE!", Color(0.7, 0.9, 1.0))
			game.sfx("blink")
			_uniq_on_evade(attacker)
			return`
tests/pvp_duel_sim.gd:506-512 `		var tier := Stats.dex_tier(f_dex, e_eva)
		if tier < 2 and randf() < float(o["eva"]):
			if tier == 0:
				return          # full miss
			grazed = true       # graze — leaks the curve's fraction through
			graze_frac = Stats.graze_through(f_dex, e_eva)`
confirmed.repro: Duel an assassin/archer that has stacked Jade (eva) gems, e.g. eva = 0.60 raw -> Stats.eva_curve = 0.50 + 0.10*EVA_OVERCAP_RATE(0.06) = 0.506. Attacker equips Amber (dex) gems to any value — 0, 200, 2000. Every strike still resolves attacker-side with e_eva = 0.0 (never a miss, never a graze), then the owner rolls a flat 50.6% dodge with no dex input. Expected per pvp_duel_sim and the Stats.dex_tier contract: at dex >= eff_eva / DEX_PER_EVA (parity) the dodge is cancelled outright (tier 2) and 100% of strikes land. Actual: ~half the strikes are voided regardless of DEX, and Amber gems buy zero offensive answer in PvP.
confirmed.fix: Carry the striker's DEX over the same seam that already carries pen: add a `dex` parameter to net_session.pvp_strike / _rpc_pvp_strike / _pvp_apply_strike (bounded with `_fin` beside the existing `pen = _fin(pen, 1.0e6, 0.0)`), pass `dex` from player_combat._hit_rival's `game.net_session().pvp_strike(...)` call, and thread it into `Player.take_damage(..., pvp_pen, pvp_dex)`. In the attacker-less branch of player.gd:1120 use the same tier logic the attacker branch gets — `var tier := Stats.dex_tier(pvp_dex, eff_eva)` and `Stats.graze_through` for the tier-1 clip — so hazards/telegraphs (pvp_dex 0.0) keep exactly today's behaviour while a duel strike is answered by DEX. No new tuning numbers are needed (DEX_PER_EVA / DEX_GRAZE_RATIO / GRAZE_CURVE_EXP already live in balance.gd).

confirmed.title: TRUE damage can be fully dodged on the attacker-less path (poison pools, telegraphs, true-typed duel strikes)
confirmed.claim: stats.gd's contract is explicit — "true" (ignores all defenses, cannot crit) — and Stats.resolve gates BOTH the evasion roll and the crit roll behind `if dmg_type != "true"` ("True damage always hits"). The attacker-less branch of Player.take_damage rolls evasion BEFORE it checks the damage type: the `dmg_type != "true"` guard sits on the resistance line (1126) and on the Mirrorstep cut (1131), but not on the dodge roll at 1121. Every attacker-less true-damage source is therefore dodgeable by an evasion build, at up to ~65% (CAP_EVA plus EVA_OVERCAP_RATE overflow).
confirmed.evidence:
player.gd:1120-1131 `	else:
		if randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):
			...
			return
		if dmg_type != "true":
			...
			amount *= (1.0 - Stats.res_frac(maxf(0.0, res - pvp_pen)))
		if dash_guard_time > 0.0 and dmg_type != "true":`
stats.gd:106-116 `		# DEX answers evasion as a TIER (dex_tier) ... True damage always hits.
		var grazed := false
		if dmg_type != "true":
			var tier := dex_tier(dex, e_eva)`
game_flow.gd:2221-2222 `				"poison":
					lp.take_damage(6.0, "true")`
confirmed.repro: Stand a hero with Jade gems (eva raw 0.50 -> eva_curve 0.50) inside a poison hazard pool (game_flow.gd:2222 ticks `take_damage(6.0, "true", attacker=null)`). Expected: 6 damage every tick, no dodge — the pool is true damage. Actual: ~half the ticks print "DODGE!" and deal 0, so the pool's DPS is halved for that build. Same path fires for a true-typed PvP strike (assassin `quietus` sets effects["type"]="true" below the HP threshold; net_session.gd:3053 lands it with attacker == null), where a dodged true hit contradicts the item card outright.
confirmed.fix: Move the type guard onto the roll: `if dmg_type != "true" and randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):` at player.gd:1121. confirmed.title: PvP brittle stacks past the balance cap and never decay (+32% permanent vs PvE's +20% for 6s)

Expected (PvE parity): stacks capped at 5 and gone 6s after the last application, so the late hit takes +0%. Actual: q.brittle sits at 8 for the whole round, so every subsequent hit — including the one 30s later — is multiplied by 1.32.

(2) Give the shell a `var brittle_t := 0.0` next to `var brittle := 0` (player_core.gd:586), stamp it `brittle_t = Balance.BRITTLE_DUR` in add_brittle, and age it in pvp.gd `_tick_rival_riders` in the shape res_shred already uses: `foe.brittle_t = maxf(0.0, foe.brittle_t - delta)` / `if foe.brittle_t <= 0.0: foe.brittle = 0`. `_clear_rival_riders` should zero `brittle_t` alongside `brittle`.

confirmed.title: Band variant authored before the "already talked" flag variant makes six NPC greetings repeatable resonance/gold faucets
confirmed.claim: `_convo_variant` returns the FIRST matching variant and evaluates each entry's `band` before its `flag` in authored order. Six greeting nodes list a `band` variant BEFORE the `<npc>_met` flag variant that carries the `"next"` short-circuit. For a player standing in that band the band variant always wins, the short-circuit never fires, and the node re-presents its full, ungated choice list on every re-talk — so the choice's resonance shift AND `_resonance_reward`'s gold drop are paid again each time. Two of the six are unbounded because the choice keeps the player inside the shadowing band.
confirmed.repro: Chapter 2, resonance >= 25 (steady band, Story.RES_BAND_AT = 25.0 at story.gd:9). Walk up to The Tracker in a social room and press E: variant 1 (`band: steady`) matches, it has no `"next"`, so `force_linear` is false (game_base.gd:1995) and both choices show. Pick "What does the edge do…": +3.0 resonance and 14 gold drop. Walk away, press E again — `ch2_tracker_met` is set but the steady variant still matches first, so the same two choices reappear. Repeat: resonance clamps at +100 (player_core.gd:49) but `res_delta != 0.0` stays true, so the 14-gold drop is an unlimited faucet. Identical loop on Gentle Suli in ch5 for 16 gold a cycle. Correct behaviour (neutral/tempted band on the tracker): the second talk ends immediately on the `ch2_tracker_met` line.
confirmed.fix: Content-side, one line moved per node — reorder the variants so each progress/`_met` flag variant sits ABOVE the `band` variant, matching the house pattern at ch4_zones.gd:275-277: in ch2_zones_side.gd swap 266<->267 and 224<->225, in ch4_zones.gd swap 417<->418, in ch5_zones.gd swap 354<->355, in promises_kept.gd move line 111 above 110, in promises_kept_2.gd move line 62 above 61. That keeps the documented "FIRST match wins" engine contract (story.gd:66-71) untouched and preserves the flavour band lines for a first meeting. Optionally add an autotest assertion that no node lists a `band` variant before a `flag` variant whose flag any of that convo's own choices sets — as a NEW `_test_*` func at the end of autotest.gd plus one call at the marked hook, never an edit to an existing section.

confirmed.title: MP-20 ready check is dropped for good if the proposal lands while a menu is open
confirmed.claim: `_on_proposal_changed` hides the ready-check card whenever any menu is open, and nothing re-renders it when the menu closes. `menus.close()` restores `game.hud.visible` but never re-drives the card, and `proposal_changed` does not fire again while the check is in flight — so a guest who happened to have the map/inventory/codex/pause screen open when `_rpc_propose` arrived never sees the Ready/Decline buttons, and the host's check dies on the 20 s timeout for the whole party.
confirmed.evidence:
hud.gd:2652-2657:
	var data: Dictionary = sess.proposal_open
	if data.is_empty() or not game.net_online() \
			or (game.menus != null and game.menus.is_open()):
		_hide_ready_card()
		return
	_show_ready_card(sess, data)

menus.gd:69-98 `close()` restores the HUD but never touches the card:
	if game and game.hud:
		game.hud.visible = game.play_started

The only emitters are the session's own transitions (net_session.gd:2858, 2877, 2888, 2917, 2943) — none of them fire on a menu close, and net_session.gd:2826 `const CHECK_TIMEOUT := 20.0` closes the check without the guest ever answering.
confirmed.repro: Co-op session, guest opens the Map (M) or Inventory (I). Host clears the chapter and presses the advance gate, which calls `propose_content("advance", …)` -> `_rpc_propose` on the guest -> `proposal_changed` emits while `menus.is_open()` is true -> `_hide_ready_card()`. Guest closes the map a second later: HUD comes back, no ready card, no way to answer. 20 s later every head gets "The ready check timed out." and the party does not advance.
confirmed.fix: Re-drive the card when the overlay clears. Add a public `Hud.refresh_ready_card()` that just calls `_on_proposal_changed()`, and call it from `menus.close()` right after `game.hud.visible = game.play_started` (menus -> hud is a sibling call through `game`, so it obeys the derived->base rule). No tuning numbers involved.

confirmed.title: Touch hit-test iterates buttons front-to-back, so the button drawn on top loses overlapping taps
confirmed.claim: `_button_at`'s doc comment promises reverse iteration so the visually-topmost (last-added) button wins an overlap, but the loop walks `_btns.keys()` in insertion order — the same order `_make_button` adds the panels in, i.e. bottom-to-top. With the shipped BTN_LAYOUT the `interact` ("Act") and `potion_next` ("⟳") circles overlap by ~20 px; `interact` is drawn on top but `potion_next` is returned first, so a tap in that lens cycles the potion loadout instead of interacting.
confirmed.repro: Mobile build, standing next to an NPC or a chest (so `game.interact_in_range` makes the Act button visible) with a multi-type potion loadout (so `potion_swap_useful()` makes ⟳ visible). Tap the part of the visible "Act" circle that lies within 40 px of (-238,-158) from the cluster origin. Expected: talk/open. Actual: the potion rotation cycles and the NPC is never engaged. The same inversion also mis-routes grabs in the layout editor, where `_button_at` picks which button a drag moves (touch_hud.gd:280).
confirmed.fix: Walk the ids in reverse so the topmost-drawn button wins, matching the comment: `var ids: Array = _btns.keys(); for i in range(ids.size() - 1, -1, -1): var id: String = ids[i]` and keep the rest of the body. (Typed local because `ids[i]` is a Variant.) No layout constants need to change.

confirmed.title: chroma.gdshader discards the node's modulate entirely, so a chroma-skinned hero shows no rage tint and no alpha changes
confirmed.claim: `fragment()` writes `COLOR` from the raw texture sample only -- it never reuses the incoming `COLOR` (which on canvas_item is modulate x TEXTURE, per the CLAUDE.md trap note) for either RGB or alpha, and it additionally hard-snaps alpha to 1.0 for any texel with a >= 0.5. The chroma material sits on `player.sprite` (skins.gd:395, applied from player_core.gd:850/861), which is the exact node player.gd re-assigns `modulate` on every frame for the berserk/rage body tint. Chromas are mutually exclusive with skins (player_core.gd:875), so the `_:` (base-class) arm of the rage match -- the one a chroma'd hero always takes -- is the arm whose colour is silently thrown away. Result: with a chroma equipped, Rage paints the aura ring but the BODY never changes colour, and any body alpha the game sets is ignored.
confirmed.repro: Play a base warrior with no skin. Cast Rage and watch the body: it goes red (player.gd:446). Now equip any warrior chroma (Skins.CHROMAS['warrior'], e.g. 'crimson', skins.gd:30) and cast Rage again: the aura ring appears but the body colour does not change at all, because the shader overwrites COLOR with the palette-swapped texture. Same for any alpha the game puts on the body while a chroma is live -- the `col.a >= 0.5 ? 1.0` branch also forces those texels opaque.
confirmed.fix: Two seams, both inside the shader + its one CPU writer. (1) Restore the modulate alpha the way silhouette.gdshader does, recovering it from the premultiplied input rather than the texture: `float mod_a = col.a > 0.001 ? COLOR.a / col.a : 0.0;` and emit `out_a * mod_a` instead of `out_a`. confirmed.title: Landmark prompt height reads the CAST SHADOW child, so `landmark_h` is always the 120.0 fallback
confirmed.claim: `landmark_node.get_child(0)` is assumed to be the structure's base sprite (the node carrying the `hpx` meta). Since the 2026-08-19 cast-shadow pass, `_add_structure` builds the cast shadow BEFORE adding the base sprite and moves it to index 0, so child 0 is the shadow copy — which never receives `wpx`/`hpx` meta. `get_meta("hpx", 120.0)` therefore always returns 120.0, and every capital landmark's interaction prompt is anchored as if the landmark were 120 px tall.
confirmed.evidence:
2483:		# The structure's rendered height (base sprite meta) — the prompt
2484:		# anchors ON the art, not at the invisible stand-point below it.
2485:		var landmark_h: float = float(landmark_node.get_child(0).get_meta("hpx", 120.0))
and in _add_structure the shadow is created first and hoisted to index 0:
3410:	if def.get("cast", true):
3411:		_prop_cast_shadow(body, base_spr, 12.0)
3412:	body.add_child(base_spr)
3129:	body.move_child(cast, 0)
`_prop_cast_shadow` copies only texture/frames/flip, never the meta (3106-3113), and no STRUCTURES def sets `"cast": false` (grep for '"cast"' in terrains.gd returns nothing), so the shadow exists for every structure whose art is taller than `CAST_SHADOW_HUG_MIN_H := 14.0`. The rest of the file already knows the shadow is a sibling: `_seal_portal` skips it by meta (201-203) and `_front_of` searches for `has_meta("wpx")` rather than taking child 0 (2247-2261).
confirmed.repro: Enter Crownfall and walk to a tall authored landmark such as `capital_sable_hall` (terrains.gd:1270, `"w": 401.1328`, so its rendered `hpx` is several hundred px). Its `uses` prompt label is placed at `-(use_dy + landmark_h * Balance.PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT)` = `-(use_dy + 120 * 0.55)` = ~66 px above the stand-point instead of ~0.55 of the real facade height. The 'E — Use' text sits at the building's footing rather than mid-facade, and the Archive's three stations all label at the same wrong height.
confirmed.fix: Add a helper beside `_front_of` in game_world.gd: `func _base_sprite_of(body: Node2D) -> Node2D:` returning the first child that `has_meta("wpx")` (else null), and rewrite `_front_of` to use it so there is one lookup. Then `var landmark_h: float = 120.0` followed by `var base := _base_sprite_of(landmark_node)` / `if base != null: landmark_h = float(base.get_meta("hpx", 120.0))` — typed var because `get_meta` is a Variant expression. The 120.0/200.0 defaults are presentation fallbacks already living here, so nothing moves to balance.gd.

confirmed.title: _apply_hazards re-fetches the whole "enemies" group inside the per-hazard loop — O(hazards x enemies) every 0.4 s
confirmed.claim: The hazard tick called from game.gd's _process (game.gd:751-753 `if hazard_tick <= 0.0: hazard_tick = 0.4; _apply_hazards()`) loops over EVERY hazard in the world (game_flow.gd:2195 `for i in range(hazards.size() - 1, -1, -1):`) and, for each ice/slow/lava patch, allocates a fresh copy of the entire enemies group and walks it. `hazards` is global, never room-scoped, and terrain pools are PERMANENT (`_add_hazard(zi, spec["type"], pos, radius, -1.0, drift)` at game_world.gd:4644, `until = -1.0` so the expiry prune at game_flow.gd:2197 never removes them), so every pool of every room the player has already left keeps paying the full scan. The type test at line 2231 also builds a throwaway Array literal per hazard per tick.
confirmed.repro: Play a chapter that visits the ice biome. terrains.gd:154 `"patches": [{"type": "ice", "count": 10, "radius": [60, 110]}]` and game_world.gd:4627 `for i in int(ceil(float(spec["count"]) * 2.0)):` put 20 permanent ice pools in every ice room; the slow biome (terrains.gd:199, count 7 -> 14) and magma (terrains.gd:148, count 4 -> 8) add more. Rooms build lazily but stay built, and their enemies stay in the group (enemy.gd:825 only freezes their _physics_process, it does not despawn them). After ~5 ice + 3 slow + 3 lava rooms the array holds ~166 physical hazards; with ~150 enemies still alive across built rooms the 2.5 Hz tick performs ~25,000 distance checks and 166 fresh Array-of-150 allocations (~25,000 refcount ops) per tick = ~62,000 iterations/s of work for pools that are rooms away from every actor.
confirmed.fix: Hoist the group once: `var mobs: Array = get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")` above the hazard loop (reuse the one already fetched at line 2190) and iterate `mobs` at 2232. Then skip hazards that cannot reach anyone: `if not active_rooms.has(int(h["zone"])) : continue` right after the expiry prune (active_rooms is the existing sim gate, game_base.gd:598, and enemy.gd:825 already uses it). Move the `["ice", "slow", "lava"]` literal to a file-level `const HAZARD_PHYSICAL := ["ice", "slow", "lava"]` so it is not rebuilt per hazard (a membership list, not a tuning number, so it stays in game_flow.gd rather than balance.gd).

confirmed.title: _think raycasts line-of-sight every physics frame for force_aggro mobs and then throws the result away
confirmed.claim: `can_see` is computed unconditionally, but both of its readers sit under a `not force_aggro` guard (line 1562 inside `if not alerted and not force_aggro:` and line 1573 inside `if not force_aggro:`). `_has_los` casts up to three physics rays and allocates an Array literal plus a PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D and a result Dictionary per ray. Because `game.wake_pack` sets `force_aggro = true` on the whole pack the moment one member notices you (game_world.gd:1477 `e.force_aggro = true`, called from enemy.gd:1568 `game.wake_pack(zone_idx, pack_id)`), essentially every mob in an active fight is in this state, so the whole cost is pure waste for the duration of every fight.
confirmed.repro: Aggro any pack. wake_pack flips force_aggro on every member, so from that frame on each of them runs the full `_has_los` on every physics tick and discards the answer. A room with 12 engaged mobs inside `aggro_range * Balance.MOB_AGGRO_KEEP` (balance.gd:1626, 1.5) burns 12 x up to 3 = 36 wasted raycasts, 12 Array literals, 36 PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D and 36 result Dictionaries per physics frame — ~2,160 wasted raycasts and ~5,000 wasted allocations per second at 60 Hz, on top of the feeler ray _avoid_obstacles already casts for the same body.
confirmed.fix: Short-circuit on force_aggro so the rays are only cast when someone reads them — behaviour-identical because both readers already require `not force_aggro`: `var can_see: bool = not force_aggro and dist <= aggro_range * Balance.MOB_AGGRO_KEEP and _has_los(player)`. No new tuning numbers, no cross-layer calls.

confirmed.title: _covering_structures walks every occluder in every built room, every render frame, per player
confirmed.claim: player.gd:9-10 `func _process(_delta): _refresh_occlusion_outline()` runs the occlusion probe every RENDER frame, and player_core.gd:1319 calls `_covering_structures()`, which fetches and walks the global `structure_occluders` group. That group is not room-scoped: every building (game_world.gd:2938, 3405, 3437), every capital backdrop (game_world.gd:3286) and every scatter obstacle (game_world.gd:3037, inside `_add_obstacle`) joins it as its room is built, and rooms stay built. The code's own comment at line 1390 admits "Every scatter prop in every BUILT room is a group member now". Worse, the get_meta default at line 1387 is evaluated EAGERLY by GDScript, so `visual.global_position` (a transform read) is computed for every candidate every frame even though the meta is always set at spawn.
confirmed.repro: Walk through a chapter. Each room adds roughly 9-14 obstacles (terrains.gd `"count"`, e.g. line 133 `"count": 14`) plus buildings/accents to the group, and nothing removes them until the world is rebuilt. After ~20 rooms the group holds several hundred Node2Ds; at 60 fps that is tens of thousands of iterations per second per player, each doing two String->StringName get_meta lookups and an eager `global_position` transform read, to find the 0-2 props actually overlapping the hero. In co-op the cost multiplies by the party size, since every Player node runs its own _process.
confirmed.fix: Two independent fixes, both local to player_core.gd. confirmed.title: Board drop-zones index by board slot while the arena renders compacted, so after a gap every zone points at the wrong token
confirmed.claim: _board_overlay places drop-zone i at `arena._slot_pos(0, i)` where i is the raw board index (0..4, nulls included). As soon as the board has a hole — which sell() and move() both create — the two indices diverge and every zone at or after the hole sits under a different token than it addresses. The comment on the two lines above the bug asserts the opposite: "drop-zones are pinned to the arena's own slot positions ... so they can never drift from where the tokens render."
confirmed.evidence:
fangmoot.gd:426-431
  static func _board_overlay(m: Menus, root: Control, mo: FangmootMoot, arena: UIFangmootArena) -> void:
  	# drop-zones are pinned to the arena's own slot positions (screen = arena-local
  	# + the topbar offset), so they can never drift from where the tokens render.
  	for i in mo.board.size():
  		var lp: Vector2 = arena._slot_pos(0, i)
  		_slot_zone(m, root, mo, i, Vector2(lp.x - 58, TOPBAR_H + lp.y - 80), Vector2(116, 150))

  func _lay_side(band: Array, side: int, uid: int) -> int:
  	var idx := 0
  	for spec in band:
  		if spec == null:
  			continue
  		uid += 1
  		_make_token(spec, side, idx, uid)
  		idx += 1

confirmed.repro: Fill board slots 0,1,2 with tokens A, B, C. Result: hovering the token you can see at the front (B) shows an empty slot with no tooltip and no drag; hovering the token drawn second (C) tooltips "Blighted Wolf — drag to reorder..." for B and dragging it to the Sell bowl sells B, not C. Clicking a tray charm card (_quick_buy -> _front_board_slot) still resolves correctly on the data side, so the mismatch is purely between what is drawn and what is clickable — the player sells and reorders the wrong tokens for the rest of the moot.
confirmed.fix: Close the gap in the moot layer so board order == render order, since the fight already ignores holes (FangmootSim._build skips null specs). Reorder intent is preserved (dragging A onto empty slot 3 gives [B, C, A] — A to the back, which is what the drop reads as). confirmed.title: Summoned tokens always render 2/2 chips regardless of their real level-scaled stats
confirmed.claim: The sim resolves a summon's stats from the owner's level (`stats: [[b,h] x3]`, e.g. the Bloom Acolyte's Rootling is [[2,2],[3,3],[4,4]]) but its "summon" log event carries only owner/uid/kind — no stats. confirmed.fix: Carry the resolved stats on the event: in fangmoot_sim.gd:533 emit `{"t": "summon", "owner": owner.uid, "uid": s.uid, "kind": s.kind, "bite": s.bite, "hide": s.hide}`, and in fangmoot_arena.gd:489 build the spec from them (`"bite": int(e.get("bite", 1)), "hide": int(e.get("hide", 1))`). confirmed.title: _test_tell_shapes() is a coroutine called without await — it runs interleaved with _test_endgame and its restore no-ops
confirmed.claim: `_test_tell_shapes` awaits (`await get_tree().process_frame` at 10010, `await get_tree().create_timer(0.35).timeout` at 10012) but is invoked without `await`, so it returns immediately and the rest of its body executes concurrently with the next section. A script scan of autotest.gd + tests/*.gd found this is the ONLY unawaited coroutine call in the suite besides the intentional `_run()` entry at line 21 — every other section is awaited. Three consequences: (a) it appends a live vargoth Boss to `game.bosses` and parents it to `game` at 10009-10010, then `_test_endgame` immediately tears the world down and rebuilds the arena — `switch_chapter` (game_world.gd:57) runs `bosses.clear()` at game_world.gd:158, so the section's own restore `game.bosses.erase(b)` (10015) is a no-op and the boss node (a child of `game`, so it survives `world.free()`) is alive inside the crucible build; (b) any of its 12 `_fail` paths report inside `_test_endgame`'s output, misattributing the failure — the exact ordering hazard the autotest doctrine warns about; (c) if any line in the resumed half errors at runtime (e.g. reading `b._tell_pose_y` on an instance a future teardown frees), the coroutine dies without ever setting `_failed`, and `_run` prints AUTOTEST PASS over a section that silently evaporated. An awaited section that errors hangs visibly instead.

dropped.title: Forced crits multiply the TRUE-damage slice, which by contract cannot crit
reasons: Code reads exactly as claimed. player_combat.gd:1266 passes only `base_amt * (1.0 - true_frac)` into Stats.resolve, whose crit roll is gated on `if dmg_type != "true":` (stats.gd:120-125), so a natural crit multiplies only the resolved slice. player_combat.gd:1276 then sums the raw true slice in (`float(result["dmg"]) + base_amt * true_frac`) BEFORE the three forced-crit riders at 1282-1296, each of which does `dmg *= crit_dmg` on the sum; their `dmg_type != "true"` guard tests the ability's overall type, not the carved-out fraction. Mirrored verbatim at 1898-1913 (_hit_rival). The contract it violates is stated in-tree at player_combat.gd:1257-1259 and classes.gd:146. Decisive corroboration the finding omitted: tests/pvp_bench.gd:236-238 models the forced-crit case as `var mult: float = crit_dmg if always_crit else xmult` / `return base * ((1.0 - tf) * mult + tf)   # true slice never crits` — the bench applies crit_dmg to (1-tf) only, so runtime and the balance model already disagree for exactly this case; a natural crit and a forced crit on the same Meteor yield different totals (1750 vs 2000), which is an inconsistency rather than a taste call. Latency also verified: true_frac is mage-only (classes.gd:146 Meteor, balance.gd:1998 axiom on the mage weapon items.gd:191, balance.gd:2005 atlas), and every force_crit/next_crit/marked_crit source is on another class or another mage weapon (player_kit_mage.gd:114 ninthstar tags the Firebolt projectile only; classes.gd:401 archer theme; classes.gd:451 assassin theme; balance.gd:2491 and 2134 archer-only) — so no shipping build manifests it today.

The code shape is real (player_combat.gd:1276 folds the true slice into `dmg` before the `dmg *= crit_dmg` riders at 1282/1287/1294, and stats.gd:120 does exclude the true slice from crit), but the defect is unreachable with the data on disk — the finding itself concedes this and its repro requires editing the balance table first. Every producer is class-locked and items.gd:61 states the equip rule ("a mage cannot wear an assassin's boots"), with player_core.gd:1216/balance.gd:2568 keying sets by `cls`. (1) `true_frac` is mage-only: classes.gd:146 (Meteor innate 0.25), balance.gd:1998 `axiom`, balance.gd:2005 `atlas`. (2) The mage's only `force_crit` is ninthstar at player_kit_mage.gd:114, written to the Firebolt PROJECTILE dict (`p.fx["force_crit"] = 1`), while Meteor builds a separate dict from the ult theme (player_kit_mage.gd:939 `eff["true_frac"] = ability_true_frac("ult")`); no mage ult theme carries force_crit. The other four force_crit sites are paladin/warlock/warrior kits and archer `herald` (player_combat.gd:1595). (3) `next_crit` is archer-only — player.gd:1031-1039 gates on `hartsbreath` / archer `uniq_set_k("C",6,"perfect_crit")` / beat `tumblearm` (balance.gd:2134 `archer_pants_Cs`), and `_hunt_rhythm_feed` (player_combat.gd:1828) is fed only from player_kit_archer.gd:115, the archer B-4pc/D-6pc set clauses, and beat `huntp` (balance.gd:2294 `archer_armor_Cs`). (4) `marked_crit` has one producer, classes.gd:451, the assassin a1 shadow theme. No player build and no test reaches the line; this is future-proofing against a data edit, not a shipping defect.

dropped.title: Lifesteal soft knee is applied twice, so overflow past the cap pays 1/100 instead of the intended 1/10
reasons:
The mechanics the finding describes are real (soft_cap is not idempotent above the cap, and it runs at player_core.gd:1805 then again at player_core.gd:2023), but the premise that a SINGLE knee on the total is the documented intent is refuted by the design doc and by a locked test.

1. The authoritative comment is not CAP_LIFESTEAL's one-liner but the cap block above soft_cap, and it explicitly enumerates TWO application points: game/scripts/balance.gd:1888-1889 `# recalc (cdr/lifesteal/combo), at consumption (current_lifesteal covers` / `# temp surges) and inside the Stats curves (crit/eva/res/greed).` That is exactly what the code does — knee the gear stat at recalc, knee again at consumption so surges cannot smuggle past. Lifesteal is the only stat with the consumption pass, and the doc names it by name.

2. The recalc knee on the RAW gear sum is a contract test, not an accident: game/scripts/autotest.gd:4107-4111 equips `"subs": {"cdr": 0.9, "lifesteal": 0.9, "combo": 0.9}` and asserts `absf(game.player.lifesteal - Balance.soft_cap(0.9, Balance.CAP_LIFESTEAL)) > 0.001` → `_fail("special-stat soft knees are off their curve")`. The proposed fix (store the raw sum at player_core.gd:1805) fails that assertion, so it is wrong as written.

3. The divergence only exists when GEAR ALONE already exceeds 0.35 — i.e. entirely inside the zone the design calls "greatly diminishing". At exactly-cap gear the two readings agree; the repro's worst case (0.50 gear + the 0.26 surge ceiling from balance.gd:1434-1435) is 0.3775 vs 0.391, ~1.4pp. That is a balance-taste nuance on an anti-degeneracy knee, not a correctness bug.

4. The stored `lifesteal` is deliberately the CAPPED, player-visible number: menus.gd:3136 `["Lifesteal", "%d%%" % int(p.lifesteal * 100), ...]` and player_core.gd:2047 print it, and the bulwark tax at player_core.gd:1904 `lifesteal *= 1.0 - uniq_gk(uniq_bw, "ls_tax")` is applied to that displayed stat — which is what the card promises. Storing the raw sum would silently change the tax's meaning and the sheet.

The double application is real and reachable, and it breaks a written invariant rather than a taste call.

MATH: `game/scripts/balance.gd:1898-1899` `static func soft_cap(v, cap, rate) -> float: return v if v <= cap else cap + (v - cap) * rate` is not idempotent above the cap. `game/scripts/player_core.gd:1805` `lifesteal = Balance.soft_cap(maxf(0.0, b["lifesteal"]), Balance.CAP_LIFESTEAL)` stores the KNEE'd value, and `player_core.gd:2023-2025` knees that stored value plus the surges again. So the gear excess converts at 0.1*0.1 = 1/100 — this even fires with NO surge active (stored 0.365 -> current_lifesteal 0.3515), so it is not surge-only.

INVARIANT BROKEN: `balance.gd:1886-1890` states the player rule "below the cap a point is a point; beyond it every point converts at SOFT_CAP_RATE (~1/10) — 'greatly diminishing', not useless", and `balance.gd:2608` `const CAP_LIFESTEAL := 0.35  # knee on the TOTAL incl. surges/berserk/pact`. The sibling stats knee'd identically in the same recalc block — `cdr` (`player_core.gd:1804`) and `combo` (`player_core.gd:1853`) — are each read raw afterwards, so only lifesteal compounds. That asymmetry is the tell that the compounding is incidental, not designed; the second knee's stated job (`player_core.gd:2020-2022`) is only to stop surges smuggling past the cap.

REACHABILITY: lifesteal is gem-only (`items.gd:1165` Vampire Eye base 0.006; `items.gd:1702-1705` `gem_value = base * lvl * (1 + 0.18*(lvl-1))` -> 0.157 at `GEM_MAX_LEVEL` 10, `items.gd:1143`) plus class passives (paladin 0.04 `classes.gd:166`, warlock 0.05 `classes.gd:179`) and tree nodes (+0.005/pt, `skills.gd:105/125/138`). Six special sockets of Lv6+ Vampire Eyes clear 0.35, so a dedicated endgame build sits past the knee — exactly the state the cap exists for, and the state `autotest.gd:4103-4111` constructs synthetically. The repro's surge value is also valid: `balance.gd:1434-1435` caps `stab_ls_amt` at 0.12+0.14 = 0.26.

MAGNITUDE: as stated, ~1.35pp in the repro; the practical harm is that an extra max-level Vampire Eye past the cap adds ~0.16pp instead of ~1.6pp. Real but low-severity, hence medium confidence rather than high.

The PROPOSED FIX is wrong as written — see corrected_fix.

dropped.title: Side-quest reward path dereferences a null player on a dedicated server
reasons: The unguarded null dereference is real and reachable, but the finding's P1 blast radius is not. Verified: game_base.gd:122-126 makes `player` a pure alias of `local_player`, and game.gd:200 `if not dedicated: player = Player.new()` (dedicated set at game.gd:71 for `--server`) leaves it null on a dedicated host. game_base.gd:1727 `var gold := int(ceil(float(reward.get("gold", 0)) * Balance.daily_gold_mult(player.level)))` reads `player.level` unconditionally — `Balance.daily_gold_mult(level: int)` at balance.gd:2856 is a typed call, so the argument evaluates even when the reward carries no gold — followed by `player.gold` (1729) and `player.faction_standing` (1732) and `player.global_position` (1764), none guarded, while the very next block guards with `if has_local_player():` (1741) and the siblings do the same (1828, 1832, 1960, 772, 800, 808, 1392). Reachability confirmed end to end: net_session.gd:2311-2326 `_rpc_flag_to_host` -> `game.net_apply_flag` -> `set_flag` -> `_check_side_quests()` (game_base.gd:1660); `sq_on_<id>` and ordinary step flags such as `mill_told` (ch2_quests.gd:29-40, still_blue steps mill_road_cleared/mill_seen/mill_told, reward gold 150) match none of game_flow.gd:679-682 KEPT_FLAG_PREFIXES nor the `cache_/hidden_/shrined_` list at game_flow.gd:760, so they are world flags and are applied on the server. REFUTED part: the repro's escalation ("execution of set_flag aborts, the loop guard stays latched, the server silently stops fanning ANY world flag for the rest of the session") is not GDScript behaviour — a null-property runtime error aborts only the erroring function, so control returns into `set_flag` at game_base.gd:1664 and `net_apply_flag` still executes `_net_flag_apply = false` at game_base.gd:1688. Actual effect is per-completion error spam on the dedicated host plus that pass of the `for id in Story.ALL_SIDE_QUESTS` loop aborting (self-healing: the next set_flag rescans every quest) and `reward["kept"]`/the toast being skipped server-side. Defect: yes. Stated P1 mechanism: no.

The null-deref shape is real (game_base.gd:1727 `Balance.daily_gold_mult(player.level)` with player null on a dedicated host per game.gd:200-204, reachable via net_session.gd:2324-2326 -> game_base.gd:1684 net_apply_flag -> set_flag -> _check_side_quests at game_base.gd:1660), and the sibling guard at game_base.gd:1826-1828 shows the omission is unintentional. But the finding's stated P1 EFFECT is refuted. (a) GDScript aborts only the erroring function frame; the error happens inside _check_side_quests, which set_flag calls at game_base.gd:1660, so set_flag resumes (1664 refresh_quest_marks, 1676 routing) and net_apply_flag still reaches `_net_flag_apply = false` at game_base.gd:1688 — the guard never latches, and the fan at net_session.gd:2326 `_rpc_set_flag.rpc(flag_name, value)` runs after net_apply_flag returns, so the server does NOT stop fanning world flags. (b) `flags["sq_paid_" + sid] = true` is written at game_base.gd:1725 BEFORE the deref, so there is no double-pay; the only skipped work is sfx/spawn_text (meaningless headless) and `set_flag(String(reward["kept"]))` at game_base.gd:1758, whose `sq_kept_` value is character-LOCAL (game_flow.gd:681, 746-751) and never routes — each guest sets its own. Net observable effect on the dedicated host is one printed engine error, no corruption, no player-visible loss. (c) Reachability is dev-only: `--server` (game.gd:67-77) is the MMO step-A authority no shipped client runs, and no test sets an `sq_on_*` flag on a server — the only server-side set_flag in the net suite is net_test_session.gd:3878 `game.set_flag("persist_probe")`. (d) The code is untouched by this branch (git diff main...HEAD on game_base.gd hunks at 662/3130/3238 only; the block dates to 3e8b89a, 2026-07-06).

dropped.title: _ensure_quest_quarry spawns a kill-step target without checking the kind exists, unlike its hunt-step twin
reasons: The code asymmetry is real (game_world.gd:1089 `Enemy.make(self, kind, ...)` with no check vs game_world.gd:1134 `if kind == "" or not Story.ALL_ENEMIES.has(kind): continue`), but it is not a defect. (a) Latent only, and unreachable by any shipped or runtime-generated data: all 10 authored kill targets resolve (ch1_quests.gd:28 wolf; ch2_quests.gd:34 blightwolf; ch3_quests.gd:25 gravewalker -> ch3_zones.gd:209; ch4_quests.gd:28 slag_brute -> ch4_zones.gd:208; ch5_quests.gd:21/45 -> ch5_zones.gd:214; ch6_quests.gd:25/48 -> ch6_zones.gd:200,204; ch7_quests.gd:31/52 -> ch7_zones.gd:202,217), and no code outside autotest fixtures writes Story.ALL_SIDE_QUESTS, so a kill target can only become bad by authoring a bug first. (b) The claimed deviation from house practice is inverted: this codebase gates authored enemy references at TEST time, not with runtime guards -- autotest.gd:5401 `if not Story.ALL_ENEMIES.has(spawn[0]): return "%s room %d: unknown enemy kind '%s'"`, :5408 for bosses, :9891-9896 for Fangmoot -- and every other authored-data Enemy.make is equally unguarded (game_world.gd:1381 room spawns, :4251 elite). The hunt guard is the outlier, not the kill path. (c) Evidence cite is also imprecise: the first unguarded index on an unknown kind is enemy.gd:509 `return Story.ALL_ENEMIES[k]` (via _setup at enemy.gd:282), not story.gd:669; tiered_level is safe (game_base.gd:713 uses .get(kind, {})).

The unguarded index exists (game_world.gd:1089 -> enemy.gd:511 `return Story.ALL_ENEMIES[k]` -> story.gd:669 `var base: Dictionary = ALL_ENEMIES[kind]`), but it is unreachable with any data in the repo, so no player or test hits the stated effect. All ten authored kill targets resolve (wolf story.gd:522, blightwolf ch2_zones_act1.gd:114, gravewalker ch3_zones.gd:209, slag_brute ch4_zones.gd:208, winterfang/hushcaller ch5_zones.gd:210/214, root_shambler/bog_lurker ch6_zones.gd:204/200, storm_harrier/void_shade ch7_zones.gd:202/217), and story.gd:1252-1274 `load_content()` merges every CONTENT_MODULES entry unconditionally, so there is no partial-load window; no kill step is built at runtime. The repro requires editing ch1_quests.gd to author a bad target, i.e. introducing the defect rather than reproducing one. The 'unlike its hunt twin' framing also inverts the convention: trusting authored kinds is the norm here (game_world.gd:1382 `var e := Enemy.make(self, spawn[0], room_pos(...) + jit, tiered_level(spawn[0], lvl))` — the room-pack spawner every player hits every room — plus ~20 boss add sites), and authored-reference integrity is enforced by TESTS, e.g. autotest.gd:5401 `if not Story.ALL_ENEMIES.has(spawn[0]): return "%s room %d: unknown enemy kind '%s'"` and autotest.gd:9893 for fangmoot tokens. The hunt guard is the outlier, and it guards nothing live: there are zero authored hunt steps in game/scripts/content/ (only the injected __hunt_test at autotest.gd:9778). Finally the proposed runtime `continue` is the wrong shape — it converts a loud authoring error into a silently uncompletable quest, the exact failure the function's own header (game_world.gd:1043-1053, 'a quest ... would be UNCOMPLETABLE') was written to prevent.

dropped.title: Inventory tab buttons silently reset the bag category filter
reasons: The mechanism is real but the impact is a UX preference, not a correctness defect. menus.gd:2038 (`inv_cat = cat`) is written on the SAME call that rebuilds the bag, so the tab lambdas at menus.gd:2046-2048 (`open_inventory("gear")` etc., cat defaulting to "all") do not desync anything: after a tab hop the bag genuinely renders unfiltered AND inv_cat=="all" correctly describes it. grep shows inv_cat has exactly one reader, menus.gd:3264 `open_inventory("gear", inv_cat)`, and that call therefore reproduces what is already on screen — so the claimed knock-on ("popovers rebuild unfiltered too") is not an independent defect. The comment at 2038 scopes the memory to the item-panel underlay rebuild, and that path works correctly. What remains is only "should a category chip selection survive a hop to Stats and back", which nothing in code, comment, or test asserts; the panel is fully torn down and re-opened on every tab press. Same for the unequip callback at menus.gd:3293. Also not a regression under review: `git log -L 2046,2048:game/scripts/menus.gd` dates the tab lambdas to 547a43b (2026-08-16) and `-L 3291,3295` dates the unequip callback to 08d6522 (2026-07-10) — neither line was touched by claude/visual-overhaul-2026-09-03.

The mechanics are as described but the defect framing is refuted on the load-bearing half, and what remains is a UI-preference call on long-standing code.

VERIFIED (mechanics): game/scripts/menus.gd:2037-2038 `func open_inventory(tab := "gear", cat := "all") -> void:` / `inv_cat = cat`, and menus.gd:2046-2048 the three `_tab(...)` callbacks call `open_inventory("gear")` / `("stats")` / `("potions")` with no `cat`, so a tab hop does rebuild at "all". menus.gd:3293 `open_inventory()` in the unequip callback likewise.

REFUTED (the consequence that makes it a bug): the claim that the tab hop "destroys the remembered one that the item-popover rebuild at line 3264 relies on" cannot happen. `inv_cat` is reassigned on EVERY entry to open_inventory (menus.gd:2038), so it is always equal to the filter the currently-rendered bag was built with — it can never go stale relative to what is on screen. menus.gd:3264 `open_inventory("gear", inv_cat)` therefore rebuilds the underlay with exactly the filter the player is looking at. I also checked the only two early-return tabs for a path that could open a popover while `inv_cat` is out of step with the visible bag: `_build_stats_tab` (menus.gd:2814, entered at 2051) and the potion tab (menus.gd:1780-2035) contain no `open_item_panel` call, so no desync path exists. The comment at menus.gd:2038 states the memory's scope precisely — "remembered so an item-panel underlay rebuild keeps the filter" — which is the only thing it is asked to do, and it does it.

WHAT IS LEFT is: clicking Stats and coming back to Gear returns the bag to the "All" chip. Nothing in code or design promises the chip survives a tab hop; returning to the same state as a fresh `open_inventory()` (game.gd:852, hud.gd:503, game_world.gd:295/455 all open unfiltered) is a defensible default, and resetting a filter on tab change is common UI behavior. No functional breakage, no data loss, no test-visible failure — a taste call.

Also not this branch's work: `inv_cat = cat` dates to e57e540 (2026-07-09), and `git diff main...HEAD -- game/scripts/menus.gd` is empty on claude/visual-overhaul-2026-09-03, so this is untouched long-standing behavior, not a regression the overhaul introduced.

dropped.title: hit_stop leaks Engine.time_scale = 0 if the Game node leaves the tree mid-freeze, permanently freezing the reloaded scene
reasons:
The code quotes are accurate (game_base.gd:3078-3085 does `return` without restoring, and `Engine.time_scale`'s only other writer is game.gd:476 — nothing re-asserts 1.0 at boot), but the finding's trigger and mechanism both fail on inspection.

(1) Two of the four cited reload sites are unreachable by construction. `hit_stop` refuses to run online — game_base.gd:3065 `if net_online() or DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless": return` — so no hit-stop is ever in flight in co-op, which kills game_flow.gd:801 (`net_host_lost`, which itself only runs `if net_online(): return`, i.e. after the session already ended) and net_session.gd:2987. The same gate makes the headless suites immune.

(2) The two solo sites need human input inside the 45-70 ms freeze. `hit_stop` also bails while paused (game_base.gd:3063 `if sec <= 0.0 or get_tree().paused: return`), and both victory paths pause the tree (game_flow.gd:2013 and 1181 `request_pause(true)`; request_pause at 649-662 does pause solo). So the pause-menu route to `exit_to_title` (menus.gd:578) can never *start* a hit-stop, and an in-flight one expires in ≤70 ms — no one navigates from an unpaused fight to the exit button in that time. The hud.gd:4671 `KEY_R` route needs a *fresh* press inside the same 70 ms, and hud.gd:4621 filters echo (`event.pressed and not event.echo`), so holding R through the kill produces no event. The repro's "any scripted/automated exit_to_title fired from the same frame as the kill" does not exist: the only non-menu caller is pvp.gd:317, behind `create_timer(Balance.PVP_END_LINGER)` and net-only.

(3) The cited mechanism is the wrong one for the stated repro. `reload_current_scene` deletes the Game node (game_flow.gd:796 comment: "the Game IS the current scene"), and a deleted instance's coroutine never resumes at all — Godot 4 aborts it in GDScriptFunctionState::resume ("Resumed function ... after await, but class instance is gone", printed in debug, contradicting "no error is printed"). The `if not is_inside_tree(): return` at game_base.gd:3082-3083 only fires for a node removed-but-alive, which no reload site produces. Consequently the finding's primary proposed fix (restore inside that bail-out) would not prevent the leak it describes.

Genuine latent hardening, yes; a defect with the stated effect and a real trigger, no.

The leak mechanism is real but the stated repro is not reachable. Two facts hold: `_hitstop_run` returns without restoring (game_base.gd:3083-3084), and nothing resets `Engine.time_scale` at boot (only writers repo-wide are game_base.gd:3073-3074/3084 and game.gd:476). But the freeze window is 45-70 ms of WALL CLOCK (balance.gd:57-59; the timer at game_base.gd:3080 is `ignore_time_scale`), and every reload site is excluded from it: (1) hit_stop hard-returns in co-op and headless — `if net_online() or DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless": return` (game_base.gd:3065-3066) — which disqualifies game_flow.gd:801 (net_host_lost, guest-only), net_session.gd:2987 (`_rpc_kicked`, guest mid-run; `net_session_over()` takes it offline and reloads in the same synchronous call, so no player physics runs in between), and pvp.gd:317 (`_finish_exit`, net-only and fired off a `PVP_END_LINGER` timer seconds after the last blow). (2) hud.gd:4671 requires `game.state == game.ST_VICTORY`; in solo the boss kill routes through the cinematic closer `run_cinematic_convo(closer_id, end_it)` (game_flow.gd:1199) so ST_VICTORY lands seconds later, and `request_pause(true)` (game_flow.gd:1181) then makes `hit_stop` early-return at game_base.gd:3063-3064 — so no hit_stop can be live when R is pressable. Even in the synchronous `end_it.call()` branch (game_flow.gd:1201) or endgame.gd:347, the R keypress would have to land inside the ≤70 ms remainder, below human reaction time. (3) game_flow.gd:771 is only reached from the pause-menu button (menus.gd:578), which needs the menu open (tree paused) plus a click — far beyond 70 ms. Also note the repro's claimed exit is wrong: `reload_current_scene` memdeletes the Game, so the coroutine is dropped and the `if not is_inside_tree()` guard at game_base.gd:3082-3083 never executes; the outcome would be the same, but the finding's primary proposed edit would not fire.

dropped.title: The occlusion outline's outer band is multiplied by an alpha that is zero exactly where that band lives, so half the shader is dead
reasons: The premultiplication math is correct — game/shaders/occluded_outline.gdshader:27 multiplies by COLOR.a, which is `texture(TEXTURE,UV).a * modulate.a`, so the band where center==0 is zeroed and the outline cannot extend past the sprite's alpha. But the claimed DEFECT (an expanded silhouette was intended and is silently lost) is refuted by the tuning record: game/scripts/balance.gd:269-274 says "Keep only a thin cool edge ... (owner 2026-07-28: full-body outline over a tombstone looked wrong, and 3.25 read too thick)" and PLAYER_OCCLUDED_OUTLINE_WIDTH was dialled 3.25 -> 1.75 against this exact shipped rendering; the shader header (:3-5) likewise describes an alpha-derived rim with a transparent interior. Growing the rim outward is the direction already rejected in-game, i.e. taste, not correctness. The claim "only inner_edge ever draws" is also overstated: outlines sample painterly art with TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR (game/scripts/player_core.gd:1337), and outer_edge = max(around-center,0) is live (and often the larger term) across the multi-texel soft-alpha feather. Residual value is a dead-branch/simplification nit only.

The stated effect is wrong on two counts. (a) `outer_edge` is not dead: `game/shaders/occluded_outline.gdshader:24-26` takes `edge = max(outer_edge, inner_edge)` BEFORE the `COLOR.a` multiply, so wherever `center` is fractional — the whole antialiased fringe — `outer_edge` is the LARGER term and dominates (center=0.3, around=1, around_min=0 gives inner=0.30 vs outer=0.70, final alpha 0.126 vs 0.054 inner-only). That fringe is not sub-texel here: the outline samples bilinearly (`game/scripts/player_core.gd:1337` `outline.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR`) on a ~0.46x downscaled body (`player_core.gd:1260` "Painterly masters render at a fractional DOWNSCALE (~0.46x world)"), so ~2.2 texels fold into each screen pixel and fractional `center` covers the visible rim. So "the entire outer band is multiplied to nothing, and only inner_edge ever draws" is false. (b) What renders is the owner-tuned target, not a silent regression: `game/scripts/balance.gd:270-274` — "Keep only a thin cool edge ... (owner 2026-07-28: full-body outline over a tombstone looked wrong, and 3.25 read too thick)" with `PLAYER_OCCLUDED_OUTLINE_WIDTH := 1.75` — the width was calibrated in-game against this exact shader, and both that comment and the shader header (`occluded_outline.gdshader:4-5`, "The sprite sheet's own alpha supplies the silhouette; the interior stays fully transparent") describe a thin on-body edge, not the "expanded silhouette" the finding asserts as intent. Scale also undercuts the repro: 1.75 texels x ~0.46 scale x 1.12 zoom (`game/scripts/game.gd:231`) is ~0.9 screen px, masked to the occluder's own pixels (`player_core.gd:1340` CLIP_CHILDREN_AND_DRAW). No player or test hits a defect; the premise about premultiplied `COLOR.a` is correct but the consequence is at most a redundant term, and the proposed fix would roughly double the band and regress the 2026-07-28 ruling.

dropped.title: The tether "bond restores it" green flash is a permanent tint -- it is set with no tween back and no timer
reasons: The mechanical half of the claim checks out — `tp.sprite.modulate = Color(0.6, 1.4, 0.5)` at game/scripts/enemy.gd:2566 has no tween/timer, and nothing re-asserts `base_mod` per frame (every `sprite.modulate = base_mod` in the file is gated on a specific state expiring: enemy.gd:930 stun, :947 windup end, :1442 the net-tell window, :1860 counter_t, :1878 reflect_t, :2445 the counter parry). But the finding's load-bearing premise — "unlike every other momentary tint in this file it is written raw with no revert" — is false, so this is the house idiom rather than a one-site oversight: `apply_slow` sets `sprite.modulate = Color(0.6, 0.8, 1.3)` at enemy.gd:2369 and NO branch restores base_mod when slow_time decays (enemy.gd:870/1449 only decrement it; the only reads are :959 and :2416), and `_martyr_wail` sets `e.sprite.modulate = Color(1.5, 0.7, 0.7)` at enemy.gd:2119 with no revert either; boss.gd sets ~20 raw tints the same way (e.g. boss.gd:830, :888, :968, :2538). The repro is also weaker than stated: the survivor is a chasing melee mob, and both the hit-flash tween (enemy.gd:2479-2481) and its own bite-windup end (enemy.gd:1667 -> :947) clear it inside a second of normal play, so the "rest of the fight" case needs the player to both stop attacking and stay out of its reach. The line is unchanged since ec5ec9f (2026-07-10) and is untouched by this branch. Net: a cosmetic stale-marker consistent with two sibling sites — whether the restored twin should keep a green "already revived" marker is a taste call, not a defect.

Mechanism verified: game/scripts/enemy.gd:2566 writes `tp.sprite.modulate = Color(0.6, 1.4, 0.5)` with no tween and no timer, and there is no restoring path that would clear it. Every `sprite.modulate = base_mod` in the file is event-gated, never a per-frame re-assert: enemy.gd:434 is one-time inside `_setup`; enemy.gd:930 fires only while `stun_time > 0.0`; enemy.gd:947 on windup expiry; enemy.gd:1442 on guest-mirror tell expiry; enemy.gd:1860/1878 on counter/reflect window expiry; enemy.gd:2445 when a counter is consumed; enemy.gd:2481/2521 are hit-flash tweens. `_apply_strip` never touches modulate. So the twin holds the green until an unrelated event stomps it, exactly as the finding states. Reachable in real play: game/scripts/content/ch6_zones.gd:206 `"root_shambler": ... "traits": ["tether"]`, ch6_zones registered at game/scripts/story.gd:1162, and pairs are linked at game/scripts/game_world.gd:1393-1400 (`a.tether_partner = b` / `b.tether_partner = a`). The repro holds: kill one twin, disengage, and the survivor chases tinted green; resuming attacks clears it via the tween at enemy.gd:2481. Effect is purely cosmetic (P3 tier as claimed). One supporting claim in the finding is false and should not be repeated: "unlike every other momentary tint in this file" — enemy.gd:2119 (`e.sprite.modulate = Color(1.5, 0.7, 0.7)` in `_martyr_wail`) is the same one-shot death cue with no revert, and enemy.gd:2369 (`sprite.modulate = Color(0.6, 0.8, 1.3)` in the slow path) is never restored when `slow_time` expires. The line is pre-existing (commit 6300a25, 2026-07-07), not introduced by this branch. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the same raw-tint idiom appears twice more in the file, so an owner could read it as house style rather than a bug.

dropped.title: The terrain LANDMARK and authored BUILDINGS add no `reserved` clearance, so scatter props are stamped into their composite footprints
reasons: The code observation is accurate but the stated effect is not a defect. game/scripts/game_world.gd:2694 (`placed.append(spos)`) and :2659 (`placed.append(bpos)`) indeed add no `reserved` entry, unlike :2470-2472 (`reserved.append({"pos": landmark_pos, "radius": float(spec.get("clearance", 190.0))})`). But (a) the resulting overlap is the game's accepted scatter tolerance, not a break: balance.gd:3211 `const SCENERY_MIN_SPACING := 120.0` is the spacing used for props that balance.gd:3253 renders at 190-230 px wide (`"tree_gnarled": 230.0`, `"tree_teal": 195.0`), so scatter trees already interpenetrate each other far more than a tree at 120 px overlaps bog_rootwell's 90 px `spore_shrine` part (terrains.gd:945-947, base `w: 210` x part `scale: 0.43`); (b) the omission is explicitly by design — game_world.gd:2454-2456 "Authored LANDMARKS ... **Unlike the terrain's shuffled structures**, these use exact room-local coordinates and reserve enough breathing room", echoed at :2811 "Empty in procedural rooms — no-op there", while the procedural landmark still self-reserves on the placing side (:2689 `if spos.distance_to(other) < 240.0`, buildings :2654 `< 260.0`); (c) there is no functional consequence — _add_structure (:3357-3359) and _add_obstacle (:2993-2995) are both `StaticBody2D` with `collision_layer = 1` / `collision_mask = 0`, so overlapping colliders throw no error and cannot pin a room, and door/road lanes are guarded separately (:2731-2734); (d) the cottage sub-claim fails on its own terms — _add_building :2947 sets `shape.size = Vector2(wpx * 0.62, 34.0)`, half-width 77.5 on a 250 px cottage, so a prop at 120 px never touches the footprint. Two supporting facts in the finding are also wrong: furnishings do not reserve real clearance by default (:2552 `float(furnish_spec.get("clearance", 0.0))` is a 0-radius no-op), and none of these lines are in this branch's diff (git diff main...HEAD on game_world.gd touches only the elite respawn at 1456 and the light-budget `szi`/`slight` change at 3459-3517). This is a long-standing tuning/taste question, not a correctness bug.

The code structure is described correctly (game/scripts/game_world.gd:2694 `placed.append(spos)` and 2659 `placed.append(bpos)` add no `reserved` entry, unlike 2470-2472 `reserved.append({"pos": landmark_pos, "radius": float(spec.get("clearance", 190.0))})`), but the claimed effect does not hold up. (1) Art overlap at 120 px is the game's shipped norm, not a defect: `Balance.SCENERY_MIN_SPACING := 120.0` (game/scripts/balance.gd:3211) gates obstacles that render at `"tree_green": 190.0, ... "tree_teal": 195.0` (balance.gd:3253,3260) through `_scenery_render_scale` in `_add_obstacle` (game_world.gd:3019-3020), so two ordinary scatter trees accepted at exactly 120 already overlap canopies by ~75 px — the balance comment "was 85 - stops 144px canopies overlapping" is stale against the hi-res widths. A prop overlapping a w:210 landmark is the same read. (2) The collider half is inert: obstacles are `collision_layer = 1` / `collision_mask = 0` (game_world.gd:2991-2992) and structures the same (game_world.gd:3361-3362), so two overlapping static mask-0 bodies never interact, log nothing, and only make a solid region solid. (3) The cited precedent is overstated - furnishings default to no clearance at all, `"radius": float(furnish_spec.get("clearance", 0.0))` (game_world.gd:2552); only hand-authored capital landmarks reserve (145-430 in game/scripts/content/capital_hub.gd:35,53,63), and their motivating bug was a corridor being sealed in a civic plaza (PROPOSALS/CAPITAL_REWORK.md:213), which cannot happen in an open procedural room. (4) The worst read is already guarded: buildings and non-tree landmarks feed `fronts` (game_world.gd:2662, 2698-2699) and `_canopy_conflict` (game_world.gd:2269-2276) rejects trees drawn behind them, while front-side overlap is deliberate ("stands in front: an overhanging crown is the natural read", game_world.gd:2273). This is a cosmetic/tuning taste call, not a defect with the stated effect.

dropped.title: `_prop_art_rect` picks the variant from ROOM-LOCAL coords while `_add_obstacle` picks it from WORLD coords — the canopy test measures a different sprite than the one placed
reasons: The seed-space mismatch is real: game/scripts/game_world.gd:2225 `var variant := Terrains.prop_variant(name, int(pos.x * 31.0 + pos.y * 17.0))` is called with ROOM-LOCAL points at 2748/2777/2828/2857, while game_world.gd:2989-2991 `Terrains.prop_variant(sprite_name, int(pos.x * 31.0 + pos.y * 17.0))` runs on the WORLD point passed at 2783 (`prop, origin + mpos`) and 2867, with `origin` = `pr.position` (2388) = `coord * ROOM_W/ROOM_H` (848, 956). Since h = native.y * s (2234) and family members differ wildly in aspect (tree_autumn 475x472 = 0.99 vs tree_autumn3 475x1469 = 3.09), a divergent variant makes the canopy rect the wrong height, which is the exact failure 2207-2216 guards against. HOWEVER the repro's magnitude is refuted: ROOM_W=2112 and ROOM_H=1248 (game_base.gd:20-21) are both divisible by 12, so the seed delta K = cx*65472 + cy*21216 is always 0 mod 2/3/4 — every family size in Terrains.PROP_VARIANT_GROUPS — and the two seeds pick the SAME variant whenever they share a sign. Simulating the real float32 Vector2 arithmetic (20k placements/room): 0.00% mismatch at coord (0,0), 0.22-1.65% at all positive-K rooms (float32 rounding of `origin + mpos` flipping the int() truncation), and only 13% at (0,-1) / 86% at (-1,0), where K goes negative and absi() flips the residue. Those negative-column rooms are reachable (spine starts at (0,0) walking E, game_world.gd:884-897; a side room can attach W of a column-0 room, 922-927), so the defect is genuine but is a few-percent-of-placements bug plus a rare whole-room bug, not "3 rooms in 4".

The seed inconsistency exists but provably cannot produce the stated effect. (a) The only variant-dependent quantity is the rect HEIGHT: game/scripts/game_world.gd:2231-2233 computes `s = SCENERY_RENDER_WIDTH[family_base] * JITTER.y / native.x` and `w = native.x * s`, i.e. `w = W*1.12`, keyed on family_base and therefore identical for every member; all eight tree families in terrains.gd:31-49 have a SCENERY_RENDER_WIDTH entry (balance.gd:3253-3260), so line 2238's `bottom = 38.0` branch always applies and line 2243 returns `Rect2(pos.x - w*0.5, pos.y + 38 - h, w, h)` — bottom edge pinned at pos.y+38 regardless of variant. (b) `_canopy_conflict` (2269-2275) only evaluates trees NORTH of a front, and a front's rect bottom is fpos.y+12 (_add_building game_world.gd:2932 `spr.position = Vector2(0, -hpx*0.5 + 12.0)` with hpx as the meta h; _add_structure 3374/3399 identical through `offset`). So `tree_top = pos.y + 38 - h < fpos.y + 12` holds for any h > 26-d, and the smallest tree render height is ~202px (deadtree 180 x 1.12); the x-overlap and `tree_bottom > front_top` tests are both h-free. Substituting tree_green (aspect 0.996) for tree_green4 (2.329), or tree_autumn (0.994) for tree_autumn3 (3.093), cannot flip the intersection. (c) The repro's premise is also wrong for the rooms the rule was written for: play_rect (game_base.gd:2247) adds room_inset_lt, which is Vector2.ZERO for every non-combat room (game_base.gd:2205-2206), and origins are exact grid multiples (game_world.gd:848, ROOM_W=2112/ROOM_H=1248), so the seed delta 65472*cx + 21216*cy is divisible by 12 while every PROP_VARIANT_GROUPS family has size 2, 3 or 4 — the two seeds select the SAME variant in the safe hubs where the cottages/stall live (the original owner bug). Only fractional-inset combat/small rooms diverge, and there the divergence is inert per (a)/(b). (d) autotest.gd:5234 `_test_canopy_fronts` already rebuilds every room and intersects the ACTUAL placed sprite rects against real fronts (metas set at game_world.gd:2909 and 3360, so it is not vacuous) and is green.

dropped.title: _amod linear-scans the whole talent tree (and allocates three empty Dictionaries per cell) 12 times per frame from the HUD
reasons: The mechanism is real but the finding is mis-quantified and its significance is not established. (a) player_core.gd:3091 `total += cell.get("amod", {}).get(slot, {}).get(field, 0.0) * tree_points[id]` contains TWO `{}` literals, not three — the third default is `0.0` — so it is 2 empty-Dictionary constructions per cell, not 3 (16 per `_amod`, not 24). (b) The claim that this per-frame cost exists "purely to render a cooldown ring and a tooltip line" ignores that the same loop already rebuilds that tooltip from scratch every frame: hud.gd:2472-2478 concatenates the tip then passes it through `_wrap_tip` (hud.gd:1876-1887), which `split("\n")`/`split(" ")`s and re-concatenates every word of every tooltip for all 5 slots — the potion tip at hud.gd:2409-2416 alone is ~90 words — plus `Art.ability_icon` (art.gd:1892) and `Classes.ability`/`theme_by_id` per slot per frame. That neighbouring identical-input work allocates at least as much as the 144 cell lookups over 12-cell tables (72 ids / 6 classes, skills.gd:24-157), so the singled-out `_amod` cost is not a bottleneck and no measurement is offered. (c) Minor: it is not uniformly 12 calls — player_core.gd:3106-3107 returns `float(ab["cd"])` for the assassin's ult before reaching `_amod`. Confirmed accurate: find_cell is an unindexed nested scan (skills.gd:160-165) with no cache, `_amod` (player_core.gd:3085-3092) calls it per allocated id, and hud.gd:2437/2472/2483 run inside the per-frame `for i in SLOTS.size():` at hud.gd:2387 driven by game.gd:658 in `_process`.

Mechanism and reachability check out exactly as claimed. `Skills.find_cell` is a nested linear scan over 12 cells/class (skills.gd:160-165, 72 cell dicts / 6 classes); `_amod` calls it once per allocated id (player_core.gd:3087-3088); `hud.update_stats` is called unconditionally from `game.gd:658` inside `_process` and has no early return before the slot loop at hud.gd:2387, where `p.ability_cost(slot)` (2437) and `p.ability_cd(slot)` (2472, 2483) give 12 `_amod` calls per frame across the 4 non-potion slots of `SLOTS` (hud.gd:273). At L40 (MAX_PER_ROW 10 x 4 rows = 40 points over up to 12 cells) an 8-id `tree_points` is realistic, so ~96 find_cell scans and ~190 empty-Dictionary constructions per frame, recomputed identically. Two corrections: line 3091 has three chained `.get` calls but only TWO `{}` defaults (the third default is `0.0`), so the allocation count is overstated by 50%; and `recalc()`/`add_tree_point` are NOT the only writers of `tree_points` (save.gd:629-632, player_core.gd:1492/1620/2531, ui/dev_panel.gd:94, bench_build.gd:226), so the optional memo would serve stale values. Scale is genuinely small — the same loop rebuilds tooltip strings, calls `_wrap_tip`, `Art.ability_icon` and `add_theme_color_override` per slot per frame, which dominate — so this is correctly a P3 micro-optimization, not a user-visible slowdown.

dropped.title: _apply_brew ignores the effect's `perm` flag for hide and both, so a one-fight buff would stick forever
reasons: The code reading is correct (game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_moot.gd:310-314 writes slot["hide"]/slot["bite"] without checking `perm`), but the claimed effect is unreachable. `eff` has exactly one origin: `fangmoot_moot.gd:247` `var brew: Dictionary = FangmootData.BREWS.get(String(card["id"]), {})` → `:250` `var eff := brew["effect"] as Dictionary`, consumed only at the two call sites `:254` and `:258`; no other code path constructs an eff for _apply_brew. In that const table (game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_data.gd:264-277) every hide/both row is perm:true — `brawlers_red` {"stat":"hide","val":2,"perm":true} (:266), `accordmark_tonic` {"stat":"both","val":1,"perm":true} (:270), `carvers_meal` {"stat":"hide","val":1,"perm":true} (:276) — and the only perm:false rows are `warding` (stat "ward", :272) and `might` (stat "bite", :274), i.e. exactly the two stats that have temporary buckets. The `ward` arm (:315-316) likewise ignores `perm` and always writes brew_ward, so the match is shaped to the table rather than general — deliberate, not an oversight. The finding itself concedes there is no live symptom; it is a latent/defensive-coding concern about data that does not exist, not a defect in shipped behaviour.

Code reading is accurate but the bug is unreachable — it is a latent-robustness note, not a live defect. `_apply_brew` (game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_moot.gd:300-316) is called from exactly two sites, both inside `buy_brew` (`:254` `_apply_brew(s, eff)` for scope "all", `:258` `_apply_brew(board[slot_idx], eff)` for scope "one"), and `eff` always comes from `var brew: Dictionary = FangmootData.BREWS.get(String(card["id"]), {})` at `:247`. `BREWS` is a `const` six-entry table (game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_data.gd:264-277); the only `"perm": false` rows are `warding` `{"stat": "ward", ...}` (`:272`) and `might` `{"stat": "bite", "val": 3, "perm": false, ...}` (`:274`), and both stats ARE routed into the one-fight buckets (`slot["brew_ward"]` `:316`, `slot["brew_bite"]` `:309`) that `_clear_one_fight_brews` (`:436-440`) wipes. Every `hide`/`both` row is `perm: true` and its desc says "permanently" (`fangmoot_data.gd:265-266, 269-270, 275-276`). No runtime path constructs a brew effect dict — `game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd:603/719/985` only read BREWS for display — and the `perm` flag on ability ops (`fangmoot_data.gd:36/69/94/151`) belongs to the separate in-fight sim path written back by `_writeback_perm` (`fangmoot_moot.gd:429-434`), not to `_apply_brew`. The repro's own first step is "add a temporary hide brew to FangmootData.BREWS", i.e. it requires authoring data that does not exist, and the finding concedes "there is no live symptom". Under the reproducibility bar no player or test can hit this.

dropped.title: Swing alternation derives its expected cycle from the same art it is meant to pin, so a lost attackc silently downgrades to a green 2-way
reasons: Confirmed by reading the code, not the summary. autotest.gd:4427 (`var expect: Array = ["attack", "attackb", "attackc"] if game.player._clips.has("attackc") else ["attack", "attackb", "attack"]`) and the identical line at autotest.gd:4472 derive the expected cycle from `game.player._clips`, the exact table player_core.gd:1020 (`if _clips.has("attackc") and _clips.has("attackb"):`) branches on. Both collapse together when the art is gone, so the assertion at 4436 (`if seen != expect`) cannot fail for a lost attackc. The gap is asymmetric and therefore not a deliberate stance: attackb is pinned three times with hard fails (autotest.gd:4419-4421 presence, 4422-4423 `!= 8` dir count, 4468-4470 for skins), and its rationale comment at 4468-4469 ("A skin missing a direction silently falls back to the single swing -- reads as a stuck strike") applies verbatim to attackc. No other gate covers it: `grep "_clips.has"` over autotest.gd + scripts/tests/*.gd returns only 4420/4427/4468/4472, and verify_art.py:105 lists attackc only in its scan tuple CLIPS, not as a required family. All three manifest bodies ship the art today (game/assets/sprites/paladin_attackc*.png, skins/elite/warrior_emberbound_heir_attackc*.png, skins/elite/assassin_erased_name_attackc*.png), so the regression the finding describes is live-reachable: drop one family and Smite/Cleave replay two motions while the suite prints ok. Confidence is medium rather than high only because this is test hardening (P2), not a shipping-code bug, and the derivation is documented in the comment at 4426 — but the claimed mechanism and effect are exactly what the code does.

The code mechanism is described accurately — Art.hero_clips probes disk (art.gd:3528 "Returns {} entries only for strips that exist on disk"), so a lost attackc family flips autotest.gd:4427's `expect` in lockstep with player_core.gd:1020 — but it is the documented, intentional contract, not a defect. CLAUDE.md:105 states the test's rule verbatim as conditional ("autotest `_test_swing_alternation` expects 3-way WHEN a body ships an attackc"), and the same paragraph (CLAUDE.md:103) plus art.gd:3487 ("attackc alone falls back to 2-way ... as before") establish the family as deliberately art-driven; autotest.gd:4444-4455 asserts the fallback as correct behavior. The manifest is a regen brief, not a claimed suite invariant. The attackb pin at autotest.gd:4420-4423 is not an inconsistency: attackb is universal across every body the loop touches, while attackc's roster is heterogeneous (of the base classes at 4416 only paladin ships one; of the skins at 4462 only two do), so deriving avoids coupling the suite to an art roster the planned skin regen is expected to move. The dir-set sub-claim also has the wrong consequence: player_core.gd:992 `if not loop and _dir_loco.has(name):` means a missing attackc dir set falls through to the flat strip loaded at 977-980 — the third motion still plays, non-directionally; it does not degrade to the single swing or a stuck strike. Reproducibility is weak: the trigger is 18 tracked PNGs vanishing or a broken import (a git-visible event that would trip the attackb pin first), asset presence/completeness is already the art lane's job (tools/preflight.py:279 check_anim_art runs diff-scoped verify_art, surfacing DIR8/GEOMETRY at 313-315), and the worst player-visible outcome is one fewer swing motion.

dropped.title: Tell-accent "drew no rim" guard is unreachable: get_child(0) is dereferenced before the child-count check
reasons: The guard is not unreachable for the condition it names. `if acc.get_child_count() < 2: return _fail("tell accent %s drew no rim")` (game/scripts/autotest.gd:9977-9978) targets a missing RIM, i.e. one child; in that case `acc.get_child(0)` at autotest.gd:9976 returns the fill Polygon2D and succeeds, and the guard fires normally. Only a zero-child return would crash first, and that state cannot occur: `_tell_accent` creates `var root := Node2D.new()` at game_base.gd:3153, unconditionally adds the fill at game_base.gd:3195-3198 (`var fill := Polygon2D.new()` ... `root.add_child(fill)`), and its only two returns are game_base.gd:3216 (ring branch, root then holds fill + 2 Line2D circles = 3 children) and game_base.gd:3224 (fill + rim = 2 children). The `match` at game_base.gd:3163 has a catch-all `_:` square arm (game_base.gd:3190), so control always reaches 3195; there is no early return and no path skipping the fill. The `as Polygon2D` sub-claim fails for the same reason: child 0 is always the fill Polygon2D, the Line2D rims are added after it. The finding's own repro requires first editing game_base.gd to introduce a return path that does not exist, so this is defensive-ordering taste in test code, not a defect with the stated effect.

The guard is NOT unreachable for the defect it names, and the finding's repro requires a hypothetical mutation of production code that no player or current test path reaches.

1) What the guard is for. Its message is "tell accent %s drew no rim" (game/scripts/autotest.gd:9978) — i.e. the one-child case: fill present, rim missing. In exactly that case line 9976 succeeds (child 0 IS the fill Polygon2D) and the count check on 9977 fires correctly. So the guard's own defect class is fully reachable and correctly reported. The finding's premise ("if `_tell_accent` ever returned a root with no children") is a different, unnamed defect.

2) The zero-child / non-Polygon2D root does not exist in the real code path. `_tell_accent` builds and parents the fill unconditionally on every branch before any return:
   game/scripts/game_base.gd:3195-3198
	var fill := Polygon2D.new()
	fill.polygon = pts
	fill.color = Color(1, 1, 1, 0.34)
	root.add_child(fill)
   The `match` above it has a catch-all `_:` arm (game_base.gd:3189, the square case), so an unknown shape cannot escape early — there is no early `return root` anywhere before 3198. Every shape then adds at least one more child: ring returns at game_base.gd:3216 after two `root.add_child(circle)` (3215) inside a two-iteration loop, all other shapes return at 3224 after `root.add_child(rim)` (3223). Child 0 is therefore always a Polygon2D, and child count is always >= 2. Both the null deref and the "silently becomes null" cast concern are unreachable as the code stands.

3) The repro is a counterfactual edit, not the code on disk. It reads "an edit to `game_base._tell_accent` ... e.g. an early `return root` on an unknown shape" — that early return does not exist, and the catch-all arm makes "unknown shape" impossible. A finding whose trigger is a future hypothetical source change is defensive-ordering taste, not a defect a player or a test run hits.

Note (not a defect, and not what the finding claims): reordering to `count check -> typed cast -> null check -> read .polygon` is a mild readability improvement, and if it is applied it should be applied for clarity only — the current lines produce identical behaviour on every input the drawer can produce.

dropped.title: full_prop_anims contract is geometry-only: a strip of four identical copies of the static passes every assertion
reasons: The claim is exactly what the code does. game/scripts/autotest.gd:4784-4816 asserts only geometry: `if int(info.get("frames", 0)) != 4` (4786), `if frame_size != static_size` (4790), `absi(frame_baselines[i] - frame_baselines[0]) > 1` (4804), `absf(frame_centres[i] - frame_centres[0]) > 2.0` (4806), plus the AnimatedSprite2D/no-nested-overlay checks (4809-4815). Frame content is never compared, so four identical copies of the static pass every branch (drift 0, sizes equal). And it is not merely latent: at commit c0838bf `"station_alchemy_t3"` was already in full_prop_anims (that revision's autotest.gd:4766) while its strip measured 0.394% under the project's own metric `motion_pct` (tools/art/audit_prop_anims.py:141-157), below `DEAD_PCT = 0.5` (line 97) — a strip the suite passed green and only the out-of-band python auditor caught. CLAUDE.md does name this block as the contract for a new rigid animated prop, so the documented in-suite gate is blind to the one defect class these props actually shipped.

The mechanical claim checks out but it is a test-hardening proposal, not a defect. game/scripts/autotest.gd:4784-4813 does assert only frames==4, frame_size==static_size, baseline drift <=1 and centre drift <=2 — four identical copies of the static would pass. But the documentation the finding leans on does not overclaim: CLAUDE.md:85 and CODING_GUIDELINES.md:153 (§40d) both spell out the autotest contract's exact scope in-line ("frame == static canvas, baseline <= 1 px, centre <= 2 px") and in the SAME sentence mandate `tools/art/audit_prop_anims.py` for every strip touched — which is precisely where the DEAD gate lives (`DEAD_PCT = 0.5` at tools/art/audit_prop_anims.py:97, `dead = base not in NO_MOTION_OK and motion_pct(p, fw) < DEAD_PCT` at :322) and where the five 2026-09-06 cases were caught and fixed. So coverage is split by design, documented, and the split is stated accurately; the finding's "the documented contract is blind" framing reads a claim into the doc that the doc does not make. Nothing is live either: I re-measured all 20 listed strips with audit's own motion_pct semantics and every one carries real motion (2.91% forge_cauldron to 52.10% banner_blue, vs a 0.5 threshold), which the finding itself concedes. No player and no current test hits anything; the scenario is a hypothetical future prop already covered by a mandatory workflow gate. Confidence is medium rather than high because the gap is factually real and audit_prop_anims is not mechanized (tools/preflight.py:280-323 check_anim_art runs verify_art only, and verify_art.py has no DEAD/motion check), so hardening the suite is a defensible improvement — just not a defect.
