COLOR.a / col.a : 0.0;` and `out_a` (hoisted out of the branches, it was duplicated) now ends `* mod_a`, so the co-op ghost's 0.4 and the downed 0.85 render again; (2) added `uniform vec3 body_tint = vec3(1.0);` multiplied into `result` AND into `col.rgb` -- the else branch matters because skins.gd:383-387 only sets chroma_active=0.0 on clear and leaves the material attached, and because protected (warm-skin/alpha-masked) texels take it inside an active chroma. Default 1,1,1 is a visual no-op, so nothing changes until a writer sets it. Deliberately did NOT recover modulate.rgb by division -- black armor texels make COLOR.rgb/col.rgb explode, which is the exact CLAUDE.md canvas_item trap ('reuse ONLY COLOR.a'); the tint therefore has to arrive as its own uniform. STILL OPEN, OUT OF THIS FILE'S SCOPE (RGB half): nothing sets body_tint yet (grep over game/scripts: no matches), so the rage/ghost/downed BODY COLOUR is still dropped for a chroma'd hero. The CPU seam the verifiers specified needs a single funnel setter on player_core.gd (where `chroma` and `sprite` already live) that writes the uniform when a chroma ShaderMaterial is attached and falls back to `sprite.modulate` otherwise -- guarded on the material being the chroma shader, NOT on `chroma != ""`, since the phantom skin swaps its own material into the same slot (player_combat.gd:455-458) -- with ALL THREE writers routed through it: player.gd:439-447 (rage + the reset to white) and player_combat.gd:913 (ghost 0.6,0.8,1.0) / :920 (downed 0.7,0.45,0.45) / :925 (reset). Also worth checking player_core.gd:1352 `outline.modulate.a = sprite.modulate.a` once that lands, and mirroring this shader edit into mobile/game/shaders/chroma.gdshader (I was told not to touch mobile/).

applied.title: sfx() cutoff tween fades and re-stamps a pooled AudioStreamPlayer already recycled for a different sound
applied.summary: Confirmed. The fade was bound to the pool NODE, not the play: game_base.gd:3040 tween_property(chosen,"volume_db",-40.0,0.4) plus an unconditional chosen.volume_db = -8.0 in the callback, while the pool is first-free round-robin (3024-3028) and hands the slot to the next sfx() the instant the roar ends. Fixed by cancelling on reuse rather than by gating the tween (a tween_property has no predicate, so the play-id idea in the sketch could not stop the ramp itself). Added `var sfx_cutoff_tweens: Dictionary = {}` beside sound_pool; at the top of sfx(), right after the slot is chosen, `var pending: Tween = sfx_cutoff_tweens.get(chosen, null)` is killed if valid and the entry erased, so taking a slot cancels its pending fade. The cutoff branch stores its tween under `chosen` and its callback now only does `chosen.stop()` + erase — no volume restore at all, since the next sfx() sets `chosen.volume_db = Balance.SFX_BASE_DB + vol_db` (that was the whole -8.0 vs -8.0+vol_db bug). The now-redundant `chosen.stream == this_stream` guard and its `this_stream` local are gone. Tuning numbers moved to balance.gd per CLAUDE.md: SFX_BASE_DB -8.0, SFX_CUTOFF_DUCK_DB -40.0, SFX_CUTOFF_FADE 0.4. Left alone deliberately: the 2.5 at boss.gd:228 (out-of-scope file, pre-existing, reads as boss-semantic) and the cutoff feature itself — the finding's premise that every roar is under 2.5 s is wrong (roar_fangmaw.ogg, roar_whitepelt.ogg, roar_gardener.wav, roar_morwen.ogg, roar_cinderhide.ogg, roar_saint_varo.wav, roar_unnamed_echo.ogg all outlive it and still need the fade), so the fade still runs for them and is only cancelled when the slot is genuinely reused. mobile/game/scripts/game_base.gd carries the same 10 lines verbatim and was NOT edited — re-sync with tools/sync_mobile.py.

applied.title: _apply_hazards re-fetches the "enemies" group inside the per-hazard loop — O(hazards x enemies) every 0.4 s
applied.summary:
Applied the two behavior-neutral parts, plus one extra neutral win; skipped the active_rooms gate.

1) Group hoist. The reset loop's fetch is now captured once — `var mobs: Array = get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")` above `for node in mobs:` (game_flow.gd:2199-2200) — and the inner enemy pass iterates that same `mobs` instead of calling `get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")` per hazard (game_flow.gd:2248). This removes one full Array-of-enemies allocation per hazard per tick. Verified safe against mid-loop kills: `enemy.gd:2541`/`enemy.gd:1524` `remove_from_group("enemies")` runs with `dying = true` set first and the node is only faded/queue_free'd (deferred), so the held reference stays valid inside the tick and the pre-existing `e == null or e.dying` guard at game_flow.gd:2250 still skips it. The `var e := node as Enemy` cast was kept rather than a typed loop var, exactly as the verifier asked.

2) Const. `const HAZARD_PHYSICAL := ["ice", "slow", "lava"]` at file level (game_flow.gd:2186), tested as `if htype in HAZARD_PHYSICAL:` (game_flow.gd:2247) — kills the per-hazard Array literal. Left in game_flow.gd, not balance.gd (membership list, not a tuning number).

3) Extra, also neutral: the patch's fields are read once per hazard into locals after the drift block (`var htype: String = h["type"]` / `hpos` / `hrad`, game_flow.gd:2222-2225) and used by both the player branch and the per-mob inner loop. Previously the inner loop did two Dictionary lookups per enemy per hazard (`h["pos"]`, `h["radius"]`) plus one per `match h["type"]`; that was the actual dominant constant factor once the allocation was gone. Placement is after the drift block (game_flow.gd:2211-2220) so a drifting pool's moved position is the one read.

NOT applied — the `active_rooms` room gate. It is not an optimization, it is a gameplay change: today an enemy parked in a room the player has left is frozen (enemy.gd:825 only early-returns from _physics_process) but still takes `e.take_damage(5.0, Vector2.ZERO, false, true)` from a lava pool every 0.4 s, so offscreen mobs standing in magma burn down and decrement zone_alive — a room can clear itself while the player is elsewhere. Gating on active_rooms silently stops that. The two reviewers also disagreed on its exact form (whether `zone < 0` hazards need an exemption; enemy.gd:1897 sows lava with the mob's own zone_idx behind an `if zone_idx >= 0:` guard, so zone -1 does not currently reach `hazards`, but that is an invariant one caller away from breaking). It needs an owner call and a full-suite run, so I left it out; items 1-3 remove the allocation storm and most of the constant factor with zero semantic risk.

Fixed UI-side, in-file, per the reviewer's alternative: new `_render_order(mo) -> PackedInt32Array` maps board index -> the arena position the arena actually draws it at (filled slots take the front positions in board order, empty slots trail behind), mirroring _lay_side exactly; _board_overlay now places zone i at `arena._slot_pos(0, order[i])`. Fixed with a pre-fight snapshot rather than new Menus state: _call captures `{"turn": mo.turn, "fangs": mo.fangs}` BEFORE call_moot and passes it through _fight_view(m, snap) -> _full_topbar(..., snap). _full_topbar derives `shown_turn`/`shown_fangs` from the snapshot (falling back to the live moot, so the shop screen at line 305 is unchanged) and uses shown_turn for both the "Turn %d" label and the new `_persona(mo, shown_turn)`. _persona gained an optional `at_turn := -1` (-1 = the moot's current turn), so its other call site in _ensure_opp is untouched. reviews.title: PvP: defender evasion is a flat, uncounterable dodge — DEX never answers it in a duel
problems: FREE I-FRAME FROM A ~0-DAMAGE GRAZE: low/mid-band DEX makes the striker WORSE than zero DEX, which inverts the fix's own claim. A tier-0 dodge returns at player.gd:1134 BEFORE the gate is armed at player.gd:1161 (`hurt_cd = 0.6`), so a dodged strike costs the striker only a retry. A tier-1 graze falls through :1136 and does arm it, and PvP strikes are non-heavy (net_session.gd:3055 `p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, false, pen, dex)` and :3057 `host_player_hit(target_pid, amount, dmg_type, 0, false, pen, dex)`), so the gate at player.gd:1024 `if hurt_cd > 0.0 and (hurt_was_heavy or not heavy):` blocks every follow-up for 0.6s. At the bottom of the band the clip is exactly zero: `graze_through` at ratio == DEX_GRAZE_RATIO computes `t = 0` then `pow(0, 1.7) = 0.0` (stats.gd:65-67), so the striker trades "dodged, retry next cd" for "0 damage, locked out 0.6s". Every fast class's a1 cd is under 0.6s (classes.gd:157 assassin 0.3, :130 archer 0.36, :143 mage 0.45, :188 warlock 0.5), so hurt_cd is the binding throttle and the loss is real, not theoretical: against 50% eva, tier 0 lands a full hit roughly every 0.9s while tier 1 near the threshold lands one every 1.2s. Midband (ratio 0.75 -> 0.5^1.7 = 0.31 leak) is about break-even. Only near parity does DEX actually pay. This is newly introduced in PvP (pre-fix every PvP evade was tier 0, so it never armed the gate), and it is a player-visible trap of exactly the kind the balance notes warn about — you buy DEX gems and your duel damage goes down.

UNDECLARED PvE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: true damage became undodgeable on the attacker-less path, which is entirely outside the PvP defect. The old code rolled the dodge unconditionally (`if randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):`); the new code wraps both the roll and the graze in `if dmg_type != "true":` at player.gd:1127. The PvP wire never sends `"true"` — `_hit_rival` folds `true_frac` into `dmg` and forwards the class dmg_type (player_combat.gd:1871, :1957, :1980) — so this clause changes nothing in duels and only bites PvE. The live caller it hits is the poison hazard, game_flow.gd:2238 `lp.take_damage(6.0, "true")`: an eva-stacked player standing in a poison pool previously dodged 50-65% of ticks and now eats every one. Defensible as consistency with stats.gd's contract, and it does de-flake several test legs, but it is a silent nerf to evasion builds that the SUMMARY does not mention at all (it only claims "only tier 0 returns as DODGE"). It should either be declared and balance-checked, or the `dmg_type != "true"` guard should wrap only the new tier logic and leave the plain dodge roll unconditional, so the change stays inside the defect.
reviews.notes:
WHAT THE FIX GETS RIGHT (verified, not assumed)

Seam is complete and both legs carry dex. `player_combat.gd:1980` `game.net_session().pvp_strike(q.peer_id, dmg, dmg_type, pen, dex)` — `dex` is the striker's own member stat (`player_core.gd:251` `var dex := 0.0`), in scope, float. Host-striker leg: `pvp_strike` -> `_pvp_apply_strike` -> `net_session.gd:3057` `host_player_hit(target_pid, amount, dmg_type, 0, false, pen, dex)` -> `net_session.gd:1324` `_rpc_player_hit.rpc_id(pid, amount, dmg_type, attacker_id, heavy, pvp_pen, pvp_dex)` -> `net_session.gd:1342-1343` `p.take_damage(..., _fin(pvp_pen, 1.0e6, 0.0), _fin(pvp_dex, 1.0e6, 0.0))`. Guest-striker leg: `_rpc_pvp_strike.rpc_id(1, ...)` -> `_pvp_apply_strike` -> `net_session.gd:3055` `p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, false, pen, dex)`. No leg drops it.

NaN/wire bounding is correct and matches the pen precedent exactly: `net_session.gd:3049` `dex = _fin(dex, 1.0e6, 0.0)` beside `pen = _fin(pen, ...)` at :3048, plus the second bound on the guest-defender leg at :1343. `_fin` (`net_session.gd:1161-1164`) returns the fallback on non-finite and clamps otherwise, so no NaN reaches `Stats.dex_tier`. Every path that reaches `take_damage`'s new param passes through one of those.

No double-dip on the graze. Attacker-side `_hit_rival` resolves against neutral defenses — `player_combat.gd:1955-1956` `Stats.resolve(base_amt * (1.0 - true_frac), dmg_type, crit, crit_dmg, 0.0, dex, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, crit_exempt)` — with `e_eva = 0.0`, `Stats.dex_tier` short-circuits to tier 2 (`stats.gd:45-46` `if eff <= 0.0: return 2`), so no roll and no graze happens attacker-side. Evasion is resolved once, owner-side.

Godot 4.4 GDScript is clean. `player.gd:1128` `var tier := Stats.dex_tier(pvp_dex, eff_eva)` infers `int` from a statically-resolvable `class_name Stats` (`stats.gd:1`) static func typed `-> int` — not the Variant-inference trap. `var pvp_grazed := false` is fine. No new signal connections, no early return that strands state (the tier-0 `return` at :1134 is the pre-existing dodge exit, unchanged). Compile gate run in the worktree: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, rc 0.

Ordering matches `Stats.resolve`. `player.gd:1141` applies res/pen, then :1143-1144 applies `amount *= Stats.graze_through(pvp_dex, eff_eva)` — the same "graze is the LAST cut" ordering as `stats.gd:135-136`. Numerically it is all multiplicative anyway, but the intent lines up.

NET_VERSION bumped for the signature change (`net_manager.gd:43`, 0.3.3 -> 0.3.4) with an accurate changelog line. No new tuning numbers; everything routes through `Balance.DEX_PER_EVA` / `DEX_GRAZE_RATIO` / `GRAZE_CURVE_EXP` via Stats.

No autotest contract is broken. `autotest.gd:362` (`take_damage(200.0, "true")`) runs after `_buff()` zeroes eva, so it read the same before and after. The `"true"` callers in `net_test_session.gd:1411/1451/1472/2386/3336` and `test_ch1.gd:427/509` all WANT the hit to land — the change makes them strictly less flaky (`net_test_session.gd:1480` literally has a `"offline lethal hit never killed (eva streak?)"` retry guard). `pvp_probe.gd` is a throwaway instrument with no asserts on this path.

WHY I WOULD NOT SHIP IT AS-IS — see `problems`. Both are real code-level consequences, not style. Neither is a crash, a desync, or a NaN; if the orchestrator decides the balance side is acceptable, the fix is otherwise structurally sound and the code would not need to be rewritten, only the graze/i-frame interaction settled and the true-damage scope creep either declared or reverted.

MINOR / NON-BLOCKING
- Redundant duplicate guard: `player.gd:1127` and `player.gd:1137` are two consecutive `if dmg_type != "true":` blocks that could be one. Harmless (`pvp_grazed` can only be true inside the first, so the ungated clip at :1143 is safe), but it reads as an artifact of patching around the existing block rather than merging.
- Mobile mirrors are drifted for all four files (`mobile/game/scripts/player.gd`, `player_combat.gd`, `net/net_session.gd`, `net/net_manager.gd` all differ from `game/`). Expected for an uncommitted tree given the branch's `sync_mobile --apply --gate` step at commit time (commit a601e1b), but it must run before staging per CLAUDE.md.
- The codex's "Evasion & DEX" note (`ui/codex.gd:1838-1841`) is written purely PvE-facing ("An evasive foe rolls its EVASION against every hit you throw") and its graze line still quotes the retired flat `Balance.GRAZE_DAMAGE` rather than the `graze_through` curve that `stats.gd:56` actually applies. The stale constant is pre-existing, not this fix's doing, but this fix is what makes the note apply to duels too — worth one line under CLAUDE.md's "ask whether the codex should reflect it".
- No test covers the new field. The 0.3.3 pen precedent shipped without one either (grep for `pvp_pen` finds zero test hits), so this is not a regression in standards — but a net_test leg asserting a parity-DEX striker cancels a high-eva defender's dodge would be cheap.

reviews.title: TRUE damage can be fully dodged on the attacker-less path
problems: NON-BLOCKING (style): game/scripts/player.gd:1127 and game/scripts/player.gd:1137 are two adjacent `if dmg_type != "true":` blocks with nothing between them. Correct, but they should be one block; the split reads like a merge artifact and invites a future edit to drop something between them.
reviews.notes:
SOUND — I would ship it.

DEFECT WAS REAL. Pre-fix, game/scripts/player.gd's attacker-less branch ran `if randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):` with no type guard, so TRUE damage rolled a full dodge. That contradicts game/scripts/stats.gd:5 (`"true" (ignores all defenses, cannot crit)`) and the identical roll's guard in the attacker path, game/scripts/stats.gd:109 `if dmg_type != "true":`.

FIX IS CORRECT. game/scripts/player.gd:1126-1136 now reads:
	var pvp_grazed := false
	if dmg_type != "true":
		var tier := Stats.dex_tier(pvp_dex, eff_eva)
		if tier < 2 and randf() < Stats.eva_curve(eff_eva):
			if tier == 0: ... return
			pvp_grazed = true
The graze multiplier at player.gd:1143-1144 is reachable only when pvp_grazed was set inside that guard, so no true-damage path touches evasion. Shape matches stats.gd:108-116 (tier-2 cancel, tier-1 graze, graze as the last cut).

REACHABLE CALL SITES CONFIRMED (all attacker-less, all previously dodgeable):
- game/scripts/game_flow.gd:2238  `lp.take_damage(6.0, "true")` (poison pool)
- game/scripts/player_core.gd:2631 `call("take_damage", max_hp * a, "true")` (BLOOD PRICE self-cost — a self-inflicted cost you could dodge for free)
- true-typed duel strikes: player_kit_assassin.gd:422/446/451 -> player_combat.gd:1980 `pvp_strike(...)` -> net_session.gd:3055 `p.take_damage(amount, dmg_type, null, false, pen, dex)`

GDSCRIPT / TRAP LIST: clean. `var tier := Stats.dex_tier(...)` infers int from a statically typed `static func dex_tier(...) -> int` (stats.gd:39); `var pvp_grazed := false` infers bool — no "cannot infer type". No new signal connections (no CONNECT_DEFERRED concern), no state stranded on an early return (the dodge `return` is pre-existing and now fires strictly less often), no new class_name, no inlined tuning number.

NaN: pvp_dex is bounded finite at both entry points — net_session.gd:1343 and net_session.gd:3048, `_fin(pvp_dex, 1.0e6, 0.0)`. Stats.dex_tier (stats.gd:45-47) and Stats.graze_through (stats.gd:57-61) both guard `eff <= 0.0` before dividing.

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE BEYOND THE DEFECT for non-PvP callers: with the new `pvp_dex := 0.0` default, dex_tier(0, eff_eva) returns 0 whenever eff_eva > 0 (ratio 0 < Balance.DEX_GRAZE_RATIO), so hazards/telegraphs/pvp.gd's forwarded DoT ticks (pvp.gd:115/123 pass no dex) keep the exact old full-dodge behaviour; when eff_eva <= 0 dex_tier returns 2 and the old `randf() < 0.0` was already false. The randf() call is now short-circuited in that case, but the global RNG is never seeded deterministically (game.gd:52 / game_base.gd:869 / game_base.gd:2986 all call randomize(); no seed() anywhere), so no determinism contract is disturbed.

NO PVP DOUBLE-DIP: player_combat.gd:1898-1899 calls `Stats.resolve(base_amt * (1.0 - true_frac), dmg_type, crit, crit_dmg, 0.0, dex, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, crit_exempt)` with e_eva = 0, so dex_tier returns 2 attacker-side and no eva/graze resolves there. Evasion and the graze exist exactly once, owner-side.

ORDERING: the graze at player.gd:1144 lands after the res/pen cut (1141) and before Mirrorstep/dr_time/flat_dr/uniq_armor — every one of those is a pure multiply (1148, 1177, 1181, 1188-1195), so the ordering is numerically identical to Stats.resolve's "graze last".

AUTOTEST: no contract broken; it removes flake. autotest.gd:362-364 asserts `take_damage(200.0, "true")` costs exactly 200 HP, and seven kill-the-player calls use true damage (tests/test_ch1.gd:427 and :509; tests/net_test_session.gd:1411, 1451, 1472, 2386, 3336). Every one could previously be voided by a dodge roll (test_base.gd:34 `_buff` zeroes dodge_time but not eva, and autotest.gd:349's comment "eva/res are zeroed by _buff" is simply wrong). They are deterministic now.

COMPILE GATE: ran `tools/Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64_console.exe --headless --path ./game --script res://check_compile.gd` -> "COMPILE OK (121 scripts)", exit 0. Changed nothing.

reviews.title: PvP brittle stacks past the balance cap and never decay
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: sound — I would ship this. Compile gate green (`COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, Godot 4.4.1, run from the worktree). Nothing changed.

DEFECT CONFIRMED (both halves real)
- Pre-fix `game/scripts/player_core.gd:645` was `brittle = mini(brittle + 1, 8)` (still visible verbatim in the un-synced mirror `mobile/game/scripts/player_core.gd:645`), against `game/scripts/balance.gd:1588 const BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS := 5`.
- Consumer `game/scripts/player_combat.gd:1945-1947`:
  `if effects.get("brittle", 0):` / `dmg *= 1.0 + q.brittle * Balance.BRITTLE_PER_STACK` / `q.add_brittle()`
  so 8 stacks x 0.04 = +32% ice amp in PvP vs the +20% the PvE path (`game/scripts/enemy.gd:2342-2343`) and the tooltip (`game/scripts/classes.gd:651-653`, "up to %d" fed by `Balance.BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS`) both promise. And there was no `brittle_t` on the Player shell at all, so nothing could age it.

THE FIX IS CORRECT AND COMPLETE
- `game/scripts/player_core.gd:587` `var brittle_t := 0.0    # its decay clock (pvp.gd ages it; enemy.gd semantics)` — sits inside the documented rider block whose header already claims "pvp.gd ticks the clocks" (`player_core.gd:566`), so no doc goes stale.
- `game/scripts/player_core.gd:646-647` now mirrors `enemy.gd:2342-2343` line for line (same `mini`, same unconditional refresh-to-full). The summary cites enemy.gd:2330/2331; the actual lines are 2342/2343 — citation drift only, enemy.gd is itself modified on this branch.
- `game/scripts/pvp.gd:106-108` is shaped exactly like the res_shred pair two lines above it and like both enemy decay sites (`enemy.gd:875-877` host sim, `enemy.gd:1454-1456` guest mirror — two paths, not a double-decay). `pvp.gd:144 foe.brittle_t = 0.0` completes `_clear_rival_riders`, whose docstring ("brittle stacks die with the round too", `pvp.gd:129`) stays true.
- Touching pvp.gd was genuinely unavoidable: without it `brittle_t` is write-only dead state.

ADVERSARIAL CHECKS, ALL CLEAR
- Godot 4.4 GDScript: no Variant-inference trap — both writes assign into already-typed vars (`int`/`float`), no `:=` on a loose expression; `mini(int, Balance.BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS)` is the identical construct enemy.gd already ships. Gate confirms.
- No NaN path: `delta` feeds `maxf(0.0, ...)` identically to the four sibling clocks; nothing divides or accumulates.
- No signals touched, so no double-connect / CONNECT_DEFERRED concern.
- No state stranded on an early return. The one asymmetry — `_tick_rival_riders` runs only in state "fight" (`pvp.gd:83-84`) — is harmless because stacks can only be CREATED in that same state: `player_combat.gd:1874` early-returns `if game == null or game.pvp == null or not bool(game.pvp.combat_live())`, and `combat_live()` is `state == "fight"` (`pvp.gd:152-153`). Create-window == decay-window, and `_clear_rival_riders` wipes at every boundary anyway (`pvp.gd:59` arm, `:242` round start, `:284` match end). The "not claimed" caveat in the summary is accurate and benign.
- Symmetric on both machines: `tick()` reaches `_tick_rival_riders` on host and guest alike (only `_start_match`/fan calls are host-gated), each aging its own attacker-side ledger.
- No autotest contract broken: `grep brittle` over `game/scripts/tests/` + `autotest.gd` returns nothing.
- Write path is still shell-only — `add_brittle` keeps its `if not _rival_shell(): return` guard (`player_core.gd:644`), and `_rival_shell()` requires `not is_locally_controlled()` (`player_core.gd:597`), so solo/co-op and your own hero stay inert. The `"brittle"` case in `net/net_session.gd:1297-1298` calls `e.add_brittle()` on an `Enemy`, not a Player, so it is untouched by this.
- CLAUDE.md compliance: the bare `8` is gone in favour of a `balance.gd` knob (the "never inline a bare tuning number" rule), and behaviour change is confined to the defect (PvP ice amp 32% -> 20%, plus stacks that now expire).

NON-BLOCKING NOTES (not defects in this fix)
- The `git diff` of `game/scripts/player_core.gd` also carries an UNRELATED sibling hunk — the `_covering_structures` reject-reorder plus `const OCCL_SORT_Y_META`/`OCCL_RADIUS_META` at `player_core.gd:678-679` and `:1389-1418`. It is not part of this fix; I checked it only for collateral damage and found none: `is_visible_in_tree()` still gates before the alpha probe, so the returned set is identical, and `var here := global_position` is hoisted out of a loop that cannot move the player. Attribute it to its own review, not this one.
- Mobile mirrors are correctly stale (`mobile/game/scripts/player_core.gd:645` still `mini(brittle + 1, 8)`, `mobile/game/scripts/pvp.gd:140` has no `brittle_t`). Per CLAUDE.md's sync policy this owes `python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate` before staging — a pending obligation the summary already flags, not a defect.
- Only the compile gate was run, as instructed; `test_quick`/`test` were not.

reviews.title: _covering_structures walks every occluder in every built room, every render frame, per player
problems: Headline overstated: this does NOT fix the stated defect, it cheapens it. The O(N)-per-render-frame-per-hero walk survives intact at player_core.gd:1398 — `get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("structure_occluders")` still allocates and returns a fresh Array of every occluder in every built room on every frame, and that allocation plus iteration is plausibly the largest single cost, untouched by the diff. The saved work is one `global_position` transform read per candidate plus one `is_visible_in_tree()` call per y/radius-rejected candidate. Ship it as a mitigation; don't let it close the ticket.

Comment inaccuracy at player_core.gd:1389-1390: "the group is global and rooms are never torn down". The group is global and rooms are never un-built (game_world.gd:1204-1206), but SCENERY is torn down and rebuilt on a terrain repaint — game_world.gd:2405-2409 `func _spawn_scenery(zi: int)` / `for node in zone_scenery.get(zi, []): if is_instance_valid(node): node.queue_free()` / `zone_scenery[zi] = []`. The operative point (every built room contributes members) holds, so this is a wording fix, not a logic error.

Stale mobile mirror: `mobile/game/scripts/player_core.gd` has zero occurrences of OCCL_SORT_Y_META, so it still carries the pre-fix loop. CLAUDE.md requires mobile/game to be re-synced from game/. That is a staging-time step for the whole 20-file batch (the tree's previous commit a601e1b did exactly that), not a defect in this hunk — but it must run before this branch is staged.

Minor citation drift in the fix summary: it cites the group joins as game_world.gd:2938, 3037, 3286, 3405, 3437 and the un-radiused capital backdrop as 3285-3286; in the current worktree those are 2974, 3073, 3322, 3441, 3473 and 3321-3322 respectively. The claims themselves verify (all five stamp occlusion_sort_y; the capital backdrop at 3321-3322 stamps sort_y and NOT occlusion_radius, so it always misses the cheap radius exit — that follow-up is real).
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SHIP IT (with caveats about the claim, not the code).

== Defect is real ==
- `game/scripts/player.gd:9-10`: `func _process(_delta: float) -> void:` / `_refresh_occlusion_outline()` — ungated, no locality/remote check (contrast `_physics_process` at player.gd:19-20, which early-returns via `_remote_present(delta)` for non-local heroes). So every Player node, local or remote, runs this every RENDER frame.
- `game/scripts/player_core.gd:1326`: `var covering: Array = _covering_structures() if sprite.visible else []` — the only gate is `sprite.visible`.
- `game/scripts/player_core.gd:1398`: `for candidate in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("structure_occluders"):` — group is global; all five join sites are in game_world.gd (2974, 3073, 3322, 3441, 3473) and `_build_room` (game_world.gd:1204-1206 `if built.get(i, false): return` / `built[i] = true`) never un-builds a room. Confirmed.

== Correctness of the applied change: clean ==
1. Set-identity preserved. All four filters (`sort_y` compare, radius compare, `is_visible_in_tree()`, probe-alpha) are pure predicates; `_visual_alpha_at` (player_core.gd:1424-1477) only reads sprite fields + a cached Image and never mutates the player or the occluder, so reordering cannot change the returned array, nor its ORDER (candidate iteration order is untouched).
2. `has_meta` swap is exactly equivalent. Old: `get_meta("occlusion_sort_y", visual.global_position.y)`. New: player_core.gd:1402-1406 `var sort_y: float` / `if visual.has_meta(OCCL_SORT_Y_META): sort_y = float(visual.get_meta(OCCL_SORT_Y_META)) else: sort_y = visual.global_position.y`. Same value in both branches. The reviewer's rejection of the naive `get_meta(..., 0.0)` variant is right — 0.0 is a legitimate world y and would silently drop occluders.
3. `var here := global_position` (player_core.gd:1397) is a Vector2 value copy and nothing in the loop moves the player; `_process` also can't race `_physics_process`. Safe hoist. `here + probe` at 1418 is byte-identical to the old `global_position + probe`.
4. The visibility reorder is a NET WIN here, not a pessimization — I checked the failure mode where most group members are hidden (then two hash lookups would run ahead of an O(1) cached `is_visible_in_tree`). It does not apply: occluders are never hidden. The only `child.visible = false` sites in game_world.gd (582, 1266, 2576) are NPC-hotspot Sprite2D children, none of which join `structure_occluders`; rooms are lazily built and left visible. So essentially every candidate is visible and the check is pure overhead until the probe stage.
5. No GDScript-38 trap hit: `var sort_y: float` declared then branch-assigned (legal, defaults 0.0); every `get_meta` result is wrapped in an annotated `float(...)`; `var here := global_position` infers off a typed Node2D property, not a Variant expression; `var reach := occl_radius + _occlusion_probe_reach` is float+float (pre-existing).
6. `const OCCL_SORT_Y_META := &"occlusion_sort_y"` / `OCCL_RADIUS_META` (player_core.gd:678-679) — no name collision anywhere in game/, no new `class_name` (so no `--import` obligation), and the StringName matches the plain-String `set_meta` literals at the five spawn sites (Godot converts both to the same StringName). These are key names, not tuning numbers, so CLAUDE.md's "no bare tuning number outside balance.gd" doesn't apply.
7. No new bug in any of the listed classes: no NaN path (no new arithmetic), no signal connect, no state stranded on an early return (`covering` is local and every `continue` leaves nothing half-written — contrast the clip bookkeeping in `_refresh_occlusion_outline`, which is untouched), no Variant inference error, no autotest contract broken (the only autotest reference to the group is game/scripts/autotest.gd:5253, a canopy-vs-front geometry read that never calls `_covering_structures`).
8. Compile gate green on the current tree: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)` (Godot 4.4.1, `--script res://check_compile.gd`).

== Why the caveats don't block ==
The change is strictly cheaper, behaviour-identical, and does not foreclose the real fix (the epoch-invalidated cache the summary describes). The two deliberate non-applications are both correctly reasoned: room-scoping to `active_rooms` would indeed drop the outline in corridors/seams where `room_at_pos` returns -1.

== Out of scope, noted only ==
The same diff carries a sibling hunk in this file (player_core.gd:587 `brittle_t`, 646-647 `Balance.BRITTLE_MAX_STACKS` / `BRITTLE_DUR`). It is a different fix; it is internally coherent (balance.gd:1588-1589 define both consts, pvp.gd:106-107,144 ages and clears `brittle_t`, mirroring enemy.gd:189,875-876) and compiles. Not reviewed further here.

reviews.title: Band variant authored before the "already talked" flag variant makes NPC greetings repeatable resonance/gold faucets (in-file scope: ch2_wander_tracker + ch2_wander_road)
problems: Line-number drift in the finding's own citations (the claims are all correct, the numbers are not). `_convo_variant` is game_base.gd:2154-2160, not 2149-2155. `var force_linear: bool = variant.has("next")` is game_base.gd:2000, not 1995. The reward call `if res_delta != 0.0: _resonance_reward(res_delta)` is game_base.gd:2026-2027, not 2019-2022. The clamp is player_core.gd:47-48, not :49. Non-blocking, but a reader following those numbers lands ~5 lines short of each cite.

Mobile mirror still carries the defect: mobile/game/scripts/content/ch2_zones_side.gd:224-225 and :266-267 remain band-before-flag. NOT this fix's fault — the branch has 20 modified game/ scripts and zero mobile changes, so `python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate` is a deferred branch-wide step. Flagging only so it is not forgotten before staging.

Scope note is accurate but understates the class. Beyond the four siblings the finding lists, a corpus grep for `"band"` across game/scripts/content shows the band-variant pattern in ~15 files (ch1_quests, ch2_aldric, ch2_factions, ch2_hub, ch2_quests, ch2_zones_act2, ch3_*, ch4_*, ch5_zones, promises_kept*). Most are quest/beat nodes whose repeat exposure differs, but the ordering hazard is structural to `_convo_variant` and worth an engine-level or lint-level sweep rather than file-by-file reorders. Out of scope for this review; not a reason to hold this fix.

Deeper fix not taken (acceptable): the root cause is that `_convo_variant` lets authoring order decide between two different kinds of predicate. A resolver that checks all `flag` variants before all `band` variants would make the whole class impossible to author wrong. The reorder is the right minimal change for this branch, but it leaves the trap live for the next author.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SHIP IT. The fix is correct, minimal, and closes the defect completely within its stated scope.

=== 1. The defect is real (verified against the engine, not the summary) ===
`game/scripts/game_base.gd:2154-2160`:
```
func _convo_variant(node: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
	for v in node.get("variants", []):
		if v.has("band") and Story.res_band(player.resonance) == String(v["band"]):
			return v
		if v.has("flag") and flags.get(String(v["flag"]), false):
			return v
	return {}
```
Both tests live in ONE loop body, so a `band` entry authored EARLIER wins over a later `flag` entry — array order, not key kind, decides. Confirmed.

`game_base.gd:2000` `var force_linear: bool = variant.has("next")` and `game_base.gd:2015` `if choices.is_empty() or force_linear:` — the band entries carry no `"next"`, so the short-circuit never fired and the full choice list re-presented.

The faucet is real and unguarded: `game/scripts/game_world.gd:1908-1913` `_spawn_wanderer` binds the NPC prompt to a bare `run_convo_id(convo_id)` with no once-flag, and `game_base.gd:1915-1937` `run_convo_id` has no repeat guard (co-op routes to `net_session.gd:2346-2350` `begin_convo`, which falls back to the same `game.run_convo` — one variant resolver, no second code path to miss). Payout on every re-talk: `game_base.gd:2026-2027` `if res_delta != 0.0: _resonance_reward(res_delta)` uses the AUTHORED delta, and `_resonance_reward` (game_base.gd:2140-2149) drops gold + a chest off `absf(delta)` — `player_core.gd:47-48` `resonance = clampf(resonance + delta, -100.0, 100.0)` clamps the stat but never the payout. Neither node's choices carry `req_not_flag` (checked lines 227-232 and 269-274), so nothing else gated the repeat.

=== 2. The diff does what it claims and nothing else ===
`git diff` is exactly four lines, two nodes. I proved it is a PURE LINE PERMUTATION (Python multiset compare of the HEAD blob vs the worktree file, CRLF-normalized: `pure permutation: True`, 292 lines both sides, zero lines only-in-HEAD / only-in-worktree). No prose was edited, no whitespace churn, no comma or indentation change — the moved lines are byte-identical to the originals.

=== 3. It fully closes both nodes ===
`ch2_zones_side.gd:224-225` (road) and `:266-267` (tracker) now put the flag entry first. Trace: iteration 1 sees a dict with no `"band"` (first `if` short-circuits on `has`), hits the `flag` test, returns the `"next": ""` entry -> `force_linear` true -> linear greeting, choices skipped, no `_resonance_reward`. Ordering alone suffices because EVERY choice in both nodes sets the flag the moved variant reads: `ch2_road_met` at :228 and :231, `ch2_tracker_met` at :270 and :273. So the second talk short-circuits in any band, including a band the player later drifts into. First-meeting flavour survives: on a first talk the flag is unset, iteration 2 reaches the band entry, and with no `"next"` the choice list still presents.

=== 4. In-file scope is complete ===
`grep -n '"band"' ch2_zones_side.gd` returns exactly two hits — 225 and 267, both fixed. The other three wanderers in the same file (`:239` ott, `:252` rell, `:281` bevin) each carry a single flag-only variant with `"next": ""`, which is the house pattern the fix converged on. Consistent.

=== 5. No new bug introduced ===
- GDScript/Godot 4.4: a reorder of two dict literals inside a `const` array. No `:=` inference, no Variant expression, no signal connect, no early return, no NaN path. None of the CLAUDE.md / §38 traps are in contact with this change.
- COMPILE GATE RUN AND GREEN: `tools/Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64_console.exe --headless --path ./game --script res://check_compile.gd` -> `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0. I ran the gate only — no suite, no scene, nothing else touched, nothing written.
- Autotest contract intact. I grepped `ch2_road_met|ch2_tracker_met|ch2_wander_road|ch2_wander_tracker` across all of `game/scripts` outside the content file: zero hits, so no test pins these nodes. The generic convo-integrity loop at `autotest.gd:1858-1863` only validates each variant's `next` target and `cue`, order-independent. Section 5c (`autotest.gd:1776-1821`) builds its own synthetic convo and is untouched. The one place a test DOES pin variant order — `autotest.gd:6467-6468`, `mute_variants[0].get("flag") == "vess_dead"` — is `ch3_wander_mute`, a different file, unaffected.
- Behaviour change is bounded to the defect: a band-qualified player who has already met the NPC now gets the short-circuit greeting instead of the band flavour + a re-openable choice list. That is the fix, and it matches how the three flag-only siblings in the same file already behave.

reviews.title: Touch mode leaves the desktop ability bar's five variant glows on screen
problems: BLOCKING: hud.gd:4410 `var n: Control = box[k] as Control` casts the slot dict's `was_ready` (bool) and `flash_ms` (int) — hud.gd:1002 — to an object type. Godot 4.4.1 OPCODE_CAST_TO_NATIVE raises 'Invalid cast: can't convert a non-object value to an object type.' under DEBUG_ENABLED and OPCODE_BREAKs, aborting set_touch_mode on the FIRST slot. Slots a2/a3/ult/potion stay fully visible on touch — worse than the five glows being fixed. Affects the editor, headless suites and the signed-debug APK (the only build that runs touch mode); only a release export degrades silently to null.

BLOCKING: the same error reddens the suites — autotest.gd:2049 calls set_touch_mode(true) inside _run_systems() (the systems tier test_quick runs) and suite_verdict.ps1:51 fails any run containing 'SCRIPT ERROR'. The compile gate cannot see it (I ran it: COMPILE OK, 121 scripts), so 'gates green' cannot have covered this edit.

FIX: use the type test, not the cast — `for k in box: if box[k] is Control: box[k].visible = not on`. OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_NATIVE yields false for non-objects with no error path, preserving the intended robustness against future keys.

MINOR: the new comment at hud.gd:4406-4408 misstates the cause — every slot node is a direct HUD child (add_child at hud.gd:945/954/966/977/992, and _label's own add_child), not just the glow; there is no bar node. The real cause was omission from a hand-maintained list.

MINOR (process): mobile/game/scripts/hud.gd:4368-4370 still holds the old 8-name list while its dict carries the same 'glow' key (mobile/game/scripts/hud.gd:1001). Touch mode is mobile-only, so the fix reaches no device until sync_mobile --apply --gate runs before staging.
reviews.notes:
DEFECT DIAGNOSIS: CORRECT. FIX AS APPLIED: NOT SHIPPABLE — it replaces a cosmetic leak with a hard runtime error that aborts the function and reddens the suite.

WHAT WAS CONFIRMED (the defect is real)
- game/scripts/hud.gd:966 `add_child(glow)` — the variant glow is a HUD child; game/scripts/hud.gd:1001 carries it in the slot dict: `slot_boxes.append({"border": border, "ring_style": ring_style, "bg": bg, "glow": glow, "icon": icon, "cd": cd, "num": num,` / :1002 `"key": key, "cost": cost, "name": name_l, "was_ready": true, "flash_ms": 0})`.
- The only other writes to it are modulate, never visible: hud.gd:2423 `box["glow"].modulate = Color(0.42, 0.46, 0.6, 0.55)`, :2464 `box["glow"].modulate = tcol if not theme.is_empty() else Color(0.42, 0.46, 0.6, 0.55)`, :2486 `box["glow"].modulate = scol`. Grep over game/ finds no `glow.visible` for slot glows. So the pre-fix 8-name list did strand five lit medallions for the whole touch session. Restoring them unconditionally on set_touch_mode(false) is also correct — desktop wants them always visible, only the tint varies.

BLOCKING BUG INTRODUCED (P0)
game/scripts/hud.gd:4409-4412:
	for k in box:
		var n: Control = box[k] as Control
		if n != null:
			n.visible = not on
The slot dict's last two entries are NOT objects: `"was_ready": true` (bool) and `"flash_ms": 0` (int) at hud.gd:1002 (still live: read/written at hud.gd:2527-2532). In Godot 4.4.1 `OPCODE_CAST_TO_NATIVE` (modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp, tag 4.4.1-stable, the exact binary in tools/Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64.exe):
	#ifdef DEBUG_ENABLED
	if (src->get_type() != Variant::OBJECT && src->get_type() != Variant::NIL) {
		err_text = "Invalid cast: can't convert a non-object value to an object type.";
		OPCODE_BREAK;
	}
	#endif
`ring_style` is a StyleBoxFlat = Variant::OBJECT, so it legitimately casts to null and the summary's reasoning holds for it — but a bool and an int trip the branch. OPCODE_BREAK is a script runtime error: it aborts set_touch_mode immediately. Godot Dictionaries keep insertion order, so the two bad keys sit last in slot 0 — slot 0's nine Controls get hidden, then the function dies and slots a2/a3/ult/potion are never touched at all. Net effect on every DEBUG_ENABLED build (editor, run_game.bat, headless suites, and the signed-debug APK that is the ONLY place touch mode runs): four whole ability slots left on screen plus SCRIPT ERROR spam — strictly worse than the five glows this was meant to fix. Only a release export (DEBUG_ENABLED off) silently returns null and behaves as intended.

The summary's stated premise — "The three non-Control entries (ring_style StyleBoxFlat, was_ready bool, flash_ms int) cast to null and are skipped by the guard, matching the typed-local pattern _pulse_slot already uses" — is wrong for the two built-ins, and _pulse_slot (hud.gd:1014-1015 `for key in ["border", "icon"]: var n: Control = box.get(key)`) is not a precedent: it hand-lists two keys that are always Nodes and never casts a bool. No other `as <ObjectType>` site in game/scripts (hud.gd:2633, :2649, :3004, :3007, :3013, :3017, :3030-3032, :3257, :3260, :3265, :3271; menus.gd:232, :1637, :2855; codex.gd:1907; fangmoot.gd:1021; touch_hud.gd:177, :208-214, :232-256, :392, :441, :620) casts a value that can be a non-object — this change is the first.

SUITE IMPACT (the gate will catch it, so "gates green" cannot have covered this edit)
- game/scripts/autotest.gd:2049 `game.hud.set_touch_mode(true)` sits inside `_run_systems()` (func at autotest.gd:70), i.e. the systems tier that even test_quick runs.
- suite_verdict.ps1:51 `$failPatterns = @('SCRIPT ERROR', 'Parse Error', 'were leaked at exit', 'RIDs of type')` fails the run on any SCRIPT ERROR line, and both test.bat and test_quick.bat route the log through it. So test_quick should go RED on this working tree.
- I ran the allowed compile gate: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`. Expected — `box[k]` is a Variant subscript, so the cast is runtime-only and the gate structurally cannot see it. Changed nothing.

MINIMAL CORRECT FORM (keeps the robust intent, no name list)
	for k in box:
		if box[k] is Control:
			box[k].visible = not on
`is` compiles to OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_NATIVE, which evaluates `object && ClassDB::is_parent_class(...)` and simply yields false for a non-object — no error path. (Equivalently: `var n: Control = box[k] if box[k] is Control else null`.)

SECONDARY, NON-BLOCKING
- The new comment's stated cause is inaccurate: "the variant glow is a direct HUD child (not a child of the bar)" implies the other slot nodes are parented under a bar. They are not — border/bg/glow/icon/cd are all direct HUD children (hud.gd:945, :954, :966, :977, :992) and num/key/cost/name come from `_label`, which ends in `add_child(l)`. There is no bar node; the real cause was simply the omission from a hand-maintained list. Fix the comment or a future reader will look for a parent that does not exist.
- CLAUDE.md mobile sync: the mirror still carries the old list — mobile/game/scripts/hud.gd:4368-4370 `for k in ["border", "bg", "icon", "cd", "num", "key", "cost", "name"]:` — while its slot dict has the same "glow" key (mobile/game/scripts/hud.gd:1001). Touch mode only exists on mobile, so the fix reaches no phone until `python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate` runs. Expected mid-work, but it must land before staging.

OTHER RISK CLASSES CHECKED, ALL CLEAN FOR THESE LINES: no NaN path; no signal connect (no CONNECT_DEFERRED concern); no early return leaving state stranded (the loop is the last statement of set_touch_mode, and set_cinematic at hud.gd:4415-4422 only touches hint_labels/avatar_root, so no interaction); no `:=` Variant-inference parse trap (the local is explicitly annotated); no autotest contract broken by the intent (autotest asserts only the touch copy strings around hud.gd's labels, not slot visibility); no behaviour change beyond glow — the loop's Control set is exactly the old 8 names plus "glow".

reviews.title: MP-20 ready check is dropped for good if the proposal lands while a menu is open
problems: NOT A BLOCKER, pre-existing hole this fix slightly widens: net_session.gd:593 `_on_session_ended` never clears `proposal_open` and never emits `proposal_changed`. A check live at session teardown therefore leaves `ready_root.visible == true` forever, and its Ready button still runs `sess.answer_ready(true)` -> `_rpc_ready.rpc_id(1, seq, ok)` (net_session.gd:2890) against a dead peer, because `answer_ready`'s own guard only tests `proposal_open.is_empty()` (net_session.gd:2883). This is already reachable WITHOUT the fix (card visible, no menu open, guest leaves the party via ESC/Leave), so the fix introduces no new class of bug -- it only adds the 'card arrived under a menu' path into the same hole. Closing it is two lines in `_on_session_ended` (`proposal_open = {}` + `proposal_changed.emit()`), which is outside the assigned file and outside this fix's scope.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: ship it. The hunk is correct, minimal, correct Godot 4.4 GDScript, CLAUDE.md-compliant, and I re-derived every load-bearing claim independently rather than trusting the summary. Compile gate green: COMPILE OK (121 scripts). Nothing in the worktree was changed.

CURRENT CODE (C:\Users\asali\Projects\MMO\.claude\worktrees\epic-panini-3fd8fd\game\scripts\hud.gd:2682-2691):
	func _on_proposal_changed() -> void:
		var sess := _chat_session()
		if sess == null or game == null:
			_hide_ready_card()
			return
		var data: Dictionary = sess.proposal_open
		if data.is_empty() or not game.net_online():
			_hide_ready_card()
			return
		_show_ready_card(sess, data)
Diff = deletion of `or (game.menus != null and game.menus.is_open())` from the second guard, plus a 6-line doc comment (hud.gd:2676-2681).

1) THE DEFECT IS REAL. Sole re-drive is the signal: hud.gd:283-284 `if mp_sess != null and not mp_sess.proposal_changed.is_connected(_on_proposal_changed): mp_sess.proposal_changed.connect(_on_proposal_changed)` is the only connect anywhere (scoped grep over game/scripts + game/*.gd). Every emitter is session-internal: net_session.gd:2859 (propose_content), :2878 (_rpc_propose), :2889 (answer_ready), :2918 (_finish_check), :2944 (_rpc_check_over). menus.close() (menus.gd:68-98) emits nothing. So a card suppressed at arrival was never rebuilt, and net_session.gd:2827 `const CHECK_TIMEOUT := 20.0`, fed to the timer at :2863, kills the check for the whole party. Confirmed exactly as claimed.

2) THE GUARD BOUGHT NOTHING - verified exhaustively, not sampled. menus.gd has exactly FOUR `root = Control.new()` sites (115, 141, 344, 1673), i.e. four shells, and every one hides the HUD layer on the line before: menus.gd:114 (_open), :140 (_open_full), :343 (open_title), :1670 (_show_class_splash). There is no fifth shell, so `is_open() == true` implies `hud.visible == false`. All seven lobby stages route through `m._open` (lobby.gd:87, 134, 207, 288, 326, 343, 439), so the lobby double-surface concern is covered by HUD visibility. menus.gd:95 `game.hud.visible = game.play_started` restores it in close(), and close() nulls `root` before the fade tween starts, so is_open() flips immediately - the card returns the same frame. menus.gd:875 (the only hud.visible=true inside menus.gd) calls close() first, so it opens no window where is_open() is true and the HUD is visible.

3) NO NEW BUG. `_show_ready_card` (hud.gd:2699-2762) is pure UI - builds labels/buttons, writes no game state, calls no sfx/pause/spawn_text - so building it under a menu has no side effect. No new signal connect (button lambdas sit on freshly created Buttons that are queue_free'd on each rebuild, hud.gd:2721-2723). No early return strands state: both exits call _hide_ready_card(). No NaN path, no float math. No Variant-inference regression - `var data: Dictionary = sess.proposal_open` is still annotated (§38a) and `game` is typed (`var game: Game`, hud.gd:6); the deleted clause held the only null-check on `game.menus`, which nothing else in the function dereferences. NO AUTOTEST CONTRACT TOUCHED: `ready_root` / `_on_proposal_changed` / `_show_ready_card` / `_hide_ready_card` appear nowhere outside hud.gd.

4) THE ONE LOAD-BEARING ENGINE ASSUMPTION, checked: an "open" card under a hidden HUD must not steal clicks from the menu. It doesn't - the HUD is a CanvasLayer (hud.gd `_ready`: `layer = 10`), and in Godot 4 CanvasLayer.visible propagates into child CanvasItems' `is_visible_in_tree()`, which is what gates Control GUI picking; a child added while the layer is hidden inherits the hidden state on ENTER_TREE. The codebase is consistent: hud.gd:4651 `if game.menus and game.menus.is_open(): return  # menus layer handles its own input` guards `_unhandled_input`, a NODE-level callback that visibility does NOT gate - a different mechanism, not a counter-example. The assumption is unasserted, but it is the same one the entire HUD already rests on.

5) CLAUDE.md / §38: no bare tuning number, no §-number in the new comment (§38i), no CONNECT_DEFERRED case, no new class_name (no --import needed), inheritance-chain rules untouched. The CLAUDE.md co-op trap ("gate on menus.is_open(), not the pause") is about INPUT gating and does not conflict - this is a display path, and HUD visibility gates its input independently of the tree pause.

MINOR, cosmetic: the new comment names three menu shells; there is a fourth (menus.gd:1670, class splash). Boot-context only, so the claim still holds.
OUT OF SCOPE, branch-level: mobile/game/scripts/hud.gd:2654 still carries the old clause - the mobile re-sync is a staging step for the whole 20-file branch, not something this hunk broke.

reviews.title: show_end_screen's title colour override is never restored, so later title cards wear it
problems: Non-blocking, durability only: the reset sits at the READER (flash_title) rather than the writer, because show_end_screen has no teardown of its own. That is complete for today's three writers, but any future code that sets title_label.text without stamping a colour re-exposes the same bug. A one-line reset inside show_end_screen's eventual dismissal, or a comment on show_end_screen (hud.gd:3711-3712) pointing at flash_title as the reset site, would close it permanently.

Housekeeping, not a defect in the fix: the mobile mirror is behind — mobile/game/scripts/hud.gd:3609-3613 still has flash_title without the reset. Expected for uncommitted round-2 work (the branch already shows a601e1b 'Mobile re-sync after the code-fix commit'), but `python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate` must run before this round is committed, per CLAUDE.md.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SOUND — would ship.

THE DEFECT IS REAL, and the claim's premise checks out end to end.
- `title_label` is built with white as an *override*, not a theme default: `game/scripts/hud.gd:696` `title_label = _label(Vector2(0, 200), 44, Color(1, 1, 1), 1280, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER)`, and `_label` at `game/scripts/hud.gd:2153` does `l.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)`. `UITheme.title(title_label, 46)` (hud.gd:697) touches only font + font_size (`game/scripts/ui_theme.gd:179-185`) — it sets no colour. So `remove_theme_color_override` would have fallen through to the engine default, not the built white. The summary's stated reason for re-stamping instead of removing is correct.
- Only three functions write that label's colour. `show_end_screen` stamps and never restores (`game/scripts/hud.gd:3712` `title_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)`); `boss_banner` stamps red at `hud.gd:3619` and restores white in its own tween callback at `hud.gd:3632`; `flash_title` previously stamped nothing. Zero `remove_theme_color_override` calls exist anywhere under `game/scripts` (Grep, 0 matches).
- The leak path is concrete: `game_flow.gd:1173`/`2011` `hud.show_end_screen("VICTORY", vtext, Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.35))`, then `advance_chapter` only zeroes alpha (`game_flow.gd:179-180` `hud.title_label.modulate.a = 0.0`) before the next card at `game_flow.gd:2049`/`game_flow.gd:79` `hud.flash_title(...)`. Pre-fix, that next chapter card rendered victory-gold. Same for the death card (`game_flow.gd:1874`), the room card (`game_world.gd:1020`) and the PvP round cards (`pvp.gd:244/255/269/272`) after `pvp.gd:300`'s DEFEAT red.

THE FIX IS CORRECT AND COMPLETE FOR TODAY'S CALLERS.
`game/scripts/hud.gd:3649` `title_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color(1, 1, 1))`, placed before `title_label.text = text` (hud.gd:3650) — byte-identical to boss_banner's restore line (hud.gd:3632). After the change all three writers stamp a colour on entry, so no consumer can inherit a stale one.

GODOT 4.4 / GDSCRIPT: clean. `title_label` is declared typed (`hud.gd:62` `var title_label: Label`), no `:=` inference on a Variant, no new signal connection, no early return that could strand the write (the reset is the first statement after `_boss_splash_shown.clear()`, and `flash_title` has no guard clauses at all). Compile gate run in this worktree: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0. Nothing changed.

NO NEW BUG.
- No behaviour change beyond the defect: nothing outside hud.gd writes this label's colour (external refs are only `hud.title_label.modulate.a` at game_flow.gd:179/215/253/2024), so no caller relied on a colour surviving into `flash_title`.
- No visible flicker: on both victory→next-chapter paths the alpha is already zeroed (game_flow.gd:179-180, 2024-2025) before `flash_title` runs, and where alpha is still 1.0 the colour and the text change on the same frame.
- No autotest contract touched — nothing in `autotest.gd` or `scripts/tests/` asserts on `title_label`, `font_color`, `flash_title` or `show_end_screen`.
- Notably it correctly does NOT use the diff's new `_set_font_color` helper (hud.gd:1910-1916). That would have been a real bug: `show_end_screen` and `boss_banner` write `add_theme_color_override` directly and bypass the helper's `"fcol"` meta, so the guard would have read a stale "already white" meta and skipped the restore. The unguarded direct write is the right call here, and `flash_title` is per-card, not per-frame, so the theme-changed reshape cost the helper exists to avoid does not apply.

reviews.title: HUD rebuilds and word-wraps every ability/buff tooltip every frame, but the text is only read on click
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: sound — I would ship it. Compile gate green (`COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`), no files modified by me.

DEFECT IS REAL AND THE FIX ADDRESSES IT
- `game/scripts/game.gd:658` `hud.update_stats(local_player)` — unconditional per-frame call, so the ability-slot loop at `game/scripts/hud.gd:2414` (`for i in SLOTS.size():`, SLOTS = 5 at hud.gd:273) and `_update_buffs()` (called at hud.gd:1185) both ran `_wrap_tip` every frame.
- Sole consumer is the click lambda: `game/scripts/hud.gd:1126` `_open_hud_popover(title, String(c.get_meta("tip", "")))`, wired at hud.gd:944 (ability border) and hud.gd:1071 (buff chip). It snapshots the text at open time, so nothing needs the wrap between clicks. Finding confirmed.

CACHE-KEY CORRECTNESS (the load-bearing question)
- `hud.gd:1896-1900`: `_set_tip` compares `String(c.get_meta("tip_raw", ""))` to `raw` and only then rewraps. `_wrap_tip` (hud.gd:1876-1886) is a pure static function of (text, width), and all four `_set_tip` callsites use the default width 56, so wrapped output is a pure function of the stored key. The cache structurally cannot desync — the rebind/theme/loadout objection is genuinely answered.
- No bypass writer: the only other `set_meta("tip", …)` calls are hud.gd:335 (cr_label), :345 (res_label), :4761 (res_label) — different controls, never passed to `_set_tip`. No `remove_meta`/`get_meta_list` anywhere in `game/scripts/`.
- Key name `tip_raw` collides with nothing (`fit_txt` hud.gd:2167, `fcol`, `full_w` are distinct).
- Controls are built once: `_build_ability_bar()`/`_build_buff_bar()` are called only from hud.gd:711-712, and `slot_boxes`/`buff_slots` are never cleared or rebuilt — so metas live as long as the HUD and the cache stays coherent for the session.

reviews.title: Touch hit-test iterates buttons front-to-back, so the button drawn on top loses overlapping taps
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: ship it. The defect is real, the fix is minimal and correct, the compile gate is green, and I found no new bug.

== 1. The defect is real (independently reproduced) ==
`_btns` insertion order and Panel child order are the SAME order, and nothing ever reorders either:
- `game/scripts/ui/touch_hud.gd:90-91` — `for id in BTN_LAYOUT.keys():` / `_make_button(String(id))`
- `:113` — `add_child(pnl)` (the only add_child of a button panel)
- `:159` — `_btns[id] = {"panel": pnl, ... "center": Vector2.ZERO}` (the ONLY write to `_btns`; grep for `_btns` shows no other assignment)
Grep over the whole file for `move_child|z_index|show_behind|top_level|remove_child|queue_free` returns NOTHING, so sibling draw order == child order == key order, permanently. Later child = drawn on top. The old `for id in _btns.keys():` therefore returned the BOTTOM-most button on any overlap — the exact inverse of the doc comment at `:385-386` ("reverse iteration so the visually-topmost (last-added) button wins any overlap"), which I confirmed is PRE-EXISTING (`git show main:game/scripts/ui/touch_hud.gd` carries the same two comment lines, and `git log main..HEAD -- game/scripts/ui/touch_hud.gd` is empty — the comment was aspirational, the code never matched it). So this is a code-vs-contract bug, not a taste call.

Geometry check (python over BTN_LAYOUT `:39-49`, BTN_D=104 `:27`, BTN_SD=80 `:28`) — exactly two circle overlaps exist, and the summary's numbers are exact:
- potion_next(-238,-158) vs interact(-180,-172): centres 59.67 px apart, radii sum 80 → 20.33 px lens. Old: potion_next (scanned first) won. New: interact (added later, drawn on top) wins.
- a2(-112,-30) vs a3(-88,-128): 100.90 apart, radii sum 104 → 3.10 px lens. Old: a2. New: a3 (drawn on top).
Every other pair clears (nearest miss: potion vs a2 at 95.7 vs 92.0). Note the potion_next/interact pair is the one that actually bites in play — `:208` and `:211-212` show both are conditionally visible, so they co-appear whenever you stand near an interactable while carrying a swappable potion, i.e. every chest/NPC in a normal run.

== 2. Correctness of the new code (Godot 4.4 GDScript) ==
`:388-390`
	var ids: Array = _btns.keys()
	for i in range(ids.size() - 1, -1, -1):
		var id: String = ids[i]
- §38a honored: both locals are explicitly annotated, not `:=`. `ids[i]` is a Variant (subscript), so `var id := ids[i]` would have been the "cannot infer type" trap; `var id: String` avoids it. The runtime cast is safe — every key is written at `:159` from `_make_button(id: String)`, fed by `String(id)` at `:91`, so `_btns` cannot hold a non-String key.
- Empty-dict edge: `range(-1, -1, -1)` is empty, so a not-yet-built `_btns` returns "" instead of erroring. No off-by-one at either end (i runs size-1 .. 0 inclusive).
- `_btns.keys()` returns a fresh Array, and `_btns` is not mutated inside the loop, so snapshotting it changes nothing.
- Compile gate run (only Godot invocation I made, as permitted): `Godot_v4.4.1 --headless --path game --script res://check_compile.gd` → `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0.

== 3. New-bug sweep — all clear ==
- NaN path: none touched; the distance test at `:394` is unchanged.
- Signals: no connect added/removed; the only connect in the file (`get_viewport().size_changed`) is untouched, so no double-connect and no CONNECT_DEFERRED concern.
- Stranded state on early return: the loop body is byte-identical (visible-skip `:392-393` then distance test `:394-395`); no state is written inside `_button_at`, so an early `return` strands nothing.
- **Hit/miss invariant preserved** — this is the key safety property. Reversal changes only WHICH id wins a lens; the SET of positions that return "" is identical. That matters at the edit-mode caller `:280` (`_drag_id = _button_at(e.position)`), whose comment at `:285` notes "a miss lets the Done/Reset buttons receive the tap": no tap that previously fell through to the Done/Reset Buttons is now swallowed, and vice versa.
- Play caller `:286` (`var id := _button_at(e.position)`): return type is still `String`, so the `:=` inference there is unaffected.
- Drag interaction: `_move_button` mutates only `b["center"]` and `panel.position`, never child order — so a player-dragged layout (`touch_layout` custom offsets, `:169-180`) keeps "drawn on top == wins the tap" consistent. The fix generalizes correctly to arbitrary player-made overlaps, which the old code did not.
- Perf: `range()` allocates an Array per call, but `_button_at` has exactly two call sites (`:280`, `:286`), both inside the `e.pressed` branch of `_on_touch` — per touch-down, not per frame. Negligible.
- Autotest contract: the only touch coverage is `_test_touch_overlay_gate` (`game/scripts/autotest.gd:6869-6934`). It drives `jp = Vector2(vp.x * 0.22, vp.y * 0.72)` (≈281,518 at 1280x720) — the left-half joystick zone, ~900 px from the bottom-right cluster. `_button_at` returns "" there before and after, so the section is order-independent and unaffected. No other test references `_button_at`.
- CLAUDE.md: no bare tuning number introduced (the -1/-1 are loop mechanics, not knobs, so no balance.gd entry needed); no codex-facing content; comment already accurate so no doc drift.

== 4. Flags (neither blocks the ship) ==
- MOBILE SYNC, confirmed and correctly scoped: `diff game/scripts/ui/touch_hud.gd mobile/game/scripts/ui/touch_hud.gd` differs ONLY in the three fixed lines, i.e. mobile still carries the buggy forward loop — and this HUD ships only on mobile/`--touch` (`game/scripts/game.gd:495-498`). BUT `git status --short mobile/` is empty for the whole branch while 20 files under `game/` are modified, so mobile is un-synced branch-wide, not specifically for this fix. It reaches devices via the normal staging ritual (`python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate`). Not editing mobile/ here was the right call under the task rules; just don't let the branch stage without that sync.
- Optional nit only: `ids.reverse()` + `for id in ids:` would be one line shorter and drop the index arithmetic, and `String(id)` at `:395` is now redundant (id is already String). Both harmless; the chosen form keeps the diff minimal and is the more type-safe of the two. Not worth a re-edit.

New code clears both. game/scripts/enemy.gd:1852 `sprite.modulate = base_mod` fires unconditionally the frame `pounce_time` crosses 0; game/scripts/enemy.gd:1859-1862 reverts on whiff expiry, matching the counter sibling at game/scripts/enemy.gd:1872 and the reflect sibling at game/scripts/enemy.gd:1890.

Retarget cadence is unchanged.

The new `base_mod` writes cannot fight `net_apply_tell` (game/scripts/enemy.gd:1495-1498) or the mirror revert at game/scripts/enemy.gd:1442.
- Net tell correctness: `net_apply_tell` does `_net_tell_t = maxf(_net_tell_t, dur)`. The purple tell (game/scripts/enemy.gd:1664, dur = MOB_LUNGE_WINDUP 0.34 + MOB_LUNGE_TIME 0.30 = 0.64) has already elapsed when the whiff tell (1.1) arrives, so maxf picks 1.1 and the yellow reverts on the same beat as the host. reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SOUND — I would ship it.

## The change (game/scripts/enemy.gd:1556-1564)
```
	var can_see: bool = not force_aggro \
		and dist <= aggro_range * Balance.MOB_AGGRO_KEEP and _has_los(player)
```
plus a 4-line comment extension at enemy.gd:1559-1562.

## 1. Does it fix the defect? Yes, and the defect is bigger than the summary claims.
`_has_los` (game/scripts/enemy.gd:1688-1701) builds a `PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D` + an Array literal and casts up to 3 `intersect_ray` calls returning a Dictionary each. `not force_aggro` short-circuits it away (GDScript `and` short-circuits; `not` binds tighter than `and`, so it parses as `(not force_aggro) and A and B`).

Two things make the waste larger than "per frame per force_aggro mob":
- `_think` is called unconditionally from `_physics_process` at game/scripts/enemy.gd:956 — no cadence gate.
- The only cull above it is game/scripts/enemy.gd:825 `if zone_idx >= 0 and not game.active_rooms.has(zone_idx): return`. **Boss adds carry `zone_idx == -1`** (comment at enemy.gd:821-822: "test dummies, boss adds, event spawns — always runs"), and boss.gd sets `add.force_aggro = true` at 7 sites (558, 824, 904, 1094, 2100, 2494, 2959). So every boss add raycasts every physics frame, forever, and discards the result. `game_world.gd:1480` `wake_pack` force_aggros a whole pack, all standing in the player's active room, i.e. all inside `aggro_range * MOB_AGGRO_KEEP` — the exact case where the old expression reached the ray.

## 2. Behaviour-identical? Verified exhaustively.
`can_see` is a function-local with exactly two readers (grep over the whole tree returns only these):
- game/scripts/enemy.gd:1566 `if dist > aggro_range or not can_see:` — inside `if not alerted and not force_aggro:` (1565).
- game/scripts/enemy.gd:1577 `if can_see:` — inside `if not force_aggro:` (1576).
Both are already unreachable when `force_aggro` is true, so forcing `can_see` false for those mobs cannot change any branch.

`_has_los` is a pure query — `direct_space_state.intersect_ray`, no assignment to any member (enemy.gd:1688-1701). Removing the call removes no side effect.

Two stale-state paths I specifically hunted and cleared:
- `los_lost_t` / `last_seen` are NOT refreshed for a force_aggro mob after the change — but they already weren't, because the whole update block sits inside `if not force_aggro:` at 1576. When force_aggro is later cleared (`game_world.gd:1199`, `game_flow.gd:1918`) the mob resumes with the same stale `last_seen` it would have had before this change. No regression.
- No cross-frame state: `can_see` is recomputed fresh each `_think`, so a force_aggro→false transition is correct on the very next frame.

No subclass reads it. `func _think` overrides exist at boss.gd:463, dummy.gd:80, dps_bench.gd:249/301, pvp_tiers.gd:145 — boss.gd:463 is a full replacement that re-derives `player`/`to_player`/`dist` itself and never calls `super`, and it has no LOS concept at all; the others return constants. Bosses are unaffected.

## 3. Correct Godot 4.4 GDScript? Yes.
- Compile gate run and green: `Godot_v4.4.1-stable --headless --path ./game --script res://check_compile.gd` → `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0.
- `force_aggro` is declared `var force_aggro := false` (game/scripts/enemy.gd:42) → statically bool, so `bool and bool and bool` matches the explicit `: bool` annotation. No §38a Variant-inference exposure (the annotation is explicit anyway).
- The backslash continuation is established house idiom, not a novelty: 542 of them in `game/scripts/**/*.gd`. The nearest structural twin is `game/scripts/game_world.gd:1478-1479` in `wake_pack` — same shape, same two-tab continuation indent, same leading `and` on the wrapped line.

## 4. CLAUDE.md / CODING_GUIDELINES §38 compliance
- No new bare tuning number (§38f) — reuses `Balance.MOB_AGGRO_KEEP`.
- No new `class_name`, no signal connection, no `_physics_process`-window spawn, no shader, no draw_colored_polygon, no autotest edit. None of the §38 traps or the CLAUDE.md trap list are in contact with this hunk.
- Comment idiom is §38i-consistent (the pre-existing "2026-07-09" anchor is preserved, no §-number references added).
- The comment addition is the right call: because `can_see` now conflates "sees" with "cares", and everything below enemy.gd:1588 is NOT force_aggro-gated, a future reader adding a `can_see` check into the movement/trait section would silently get false for every engaged mob. The comment names that trap explicitly.

## 5. New bugs introduced? None found.
Checked and cleared: NaN path (untouched — `dist` handling unchanged, and the `is_finite` scrub at enemy.gd:850-855 sits above), double-connected signals (none), state stranded on an early return (the `return _drift_home()` at 1567 and 1585 are both already inside `not force_aggro` guards, unreachable for the affected mobs), Variant inference (explicit annotation, statically-typed operands), autotest contracts (`autotest.gd:4392` `_test_single_idle_walk_strip` sets `force_aggro = true` + `zone_idx = -1` and asserts the walk strip advances — it now skips the leash block exactly as before and falls through to normal AI; `autotest.gd:5207-5212` and `test_ch1.gd:142/156/158` only read the `alerted`/`force_aggro` flags themselves, never LOS).

## 6. Mobile
Confirmed the claim: `mobile/game/scripts/enemy.gd:1560` still carries the old single-line form, and `git status --short mobile/` is empty. That is the correct CLAUDE.md posture (game/ is source of truth; the re-sync is the stager's `python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate` step), not a defect in this fix.

reviews.notes:
SOUND — ship it, with two comment corrections and one owner-visible side effect to flag.

CORRECTNESS OF THE ALPHA FIX (the half that is actually implemented): correct. game/shaders/chroma.gdshader:42-43 `float mod_a = col.a > 0.001 ? COLOR.a / col.a : 0.0; float out_a = (col.a >= 0.5 ? 1.0 : col.a) * mod_a;`. Godot canvas_item initializes COLOR = texture(TEXTURE,UV) * vertex modulate, so COLOR.a/col.a is exactly modulate.a; both sides read the same filtered texture sample so the ratio is exact regardless of filtering. Division is guarded (no NaN/Inf); below the guard out_a becomes 0 where the old code emitted <=0.001, i.e. invisible either way. Hoisting out_a out of the two branches removes the duplication and both exits now compose it identically.

THE DEFECT IS REAL AND THIS FIXES IT: the two down-states are NOT stomped by the per-frame alpha seam — game/scripts/player.gd:212-216 early-returns while `downed or ghost` (`if downed or ghost:` ... `_down_tick(delta)` / `return`), so player_combat.gd:913 `sprite.modulate = Color(0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 0.4)` and :920 `Color(0.7, 0.45, 0.45, 0.85)` reach the material set at skins.gd:395 and were previously forced opaque. skin_vanish (player.gd:384 `sprite.modulate.a = skin_vanish_alpha`, used by player_kit_warrior.gd:365-367's 0.16 phase-out) is fixed too.

CLEARED AS NON-ISSUES: no GDScript changed, so the Variant-inference / double-connected-signal / stranded-state-on-early-return classes do not apply; no autotest contract touches this (grep chroma over game/scripts/tests + game/autotest.gd = 0 hits); Godot 4 shading syntax is valid (ternary, vec3 uniform default, vec4(vec3,float)); body_tint default vec3(1.0) is a strict no-op; the else branch genuinely matters because skins.gd:383-387 sets chroma_active=0.0 on clear and leaves the material attached. The compile gate CANNOT validate this change — game/check_compile.gd:19,40 only walks files ending ".gd" — so running it would give zero signal for a .gdshader; I verified syntax by inspection instead and changed nothing.

WHY I STILL SAY SHIP: strictly an improvement, no regression path found, guarded division, identity-default uniform. The remaining RGB half (rage tint still dropped) is honestly scoped out and its reasoning is right — recovering modulate.rgb by division is exactly the CLAUDE.md canvas_item trap on black armour texels.

reviews.title: sfx() cutoff tween fades and re-stamps a pooled AudioStreamPlayer already recycled for a different sound
problems: NIT (not a ship-blocker): game/scripts/game.gd:114 `sp.volume_db = -8.0` still hard-codes the same base level the fix just named `Balance.SFX_BASE_DB`. Harmless today because sfx() overwrites volume_db before every play, so the two can never disagree audibly — but it is now a duplicated tuning constant one file away from its home, and preflight's balance-number lint is diff-scoped so it will never flag it. One-line follow-up.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: ship it. The fix is real, minimal, correct Godot 4.4 GDScript, and I found no new bug. Compile gate run in the worktree: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0.

DEFECT CONFIRMED (pre-fix, still verbatim in the unsynced mirror `mobile/game/scripts/game_base.gd:3037-3044`):
  var this_stream: AudioStream = chosen.stream
  var tween := create_tween()
  tween.tween_interval(cutoff)
  tween.tween_property(chosen, "volume_db", -40.0, 0.4)
  tween.tween_callback(func() -> void:
      if chosen.stream == this_stream:
          chosen.stop()
      chosen.volume_db = -8.0
  )
The `this_stream` guard only protected `stop()`. The `tween_property` ramp and the `volume_db = -8.0` restamp were unconditional, and Godot 4's PropertyTweener captures its from-value when the tweener STARTS (not at create time), so a slot recycled during the interval gets ducked to -40 dB over 0.4 s and then hard-set to -8.0, discarding the new play's `vol_db` offset. Reuse is trivially reachable: the pool is first-free round-robin (game/scripts/game_base.gd:3029-3033 `var chosen: AudioStreamPlayer = sound_pool[0]` / `for sp in sound_pool: if not sp.playing: chosen = sp; break`) over only 10 players (game/scripts/game.gd:112-117 `for i in 10:`), so a roar shorter than its 2.5 s cutoff frees its slot immediately.

SCOPE: exactly one caller passes cutoff — game/scripts/boss.gd:228 `game.sfx(key if game.sounds.has(key) else "roar", 1.0, 2.5)`. Grepped every other `sfx(` call site; all pass `0.0` or omit it. So this is boss-roar-only, matching the summary.

THE FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE. Cancel-on-reuse (game_base.gd:3034-3040) rather than a predicate inside the callback is correct, because there is no way to abort an already-running `tween_property` from inside a callback — the ramp is the damaging half and a play-id check in the callback would not have stopped it. Placement is right: after the slot is chosen (3029-3033), before anything is written to it (3044-3047), and with no early return in between (the only `return` is at 3027-3028, before slot selection), so no half-mutated state is stranded.

CORRECTNESS CHECKS I RAN AND THEY PASS:
- Variant inference trap (CLAUDE.md): `var pending: Tween = sfx_cutoff_tweens.get(chosen, null)` (3037) is explicitly annotated. `Dictionary.get` returns Variant; `:=` here would have been the classic parse error. Correct.
- `pending != null and pending.is_valid()` (3038) — `Tween.is_valid()` exists in 4.x and returns false for a finished/killed tween, so `kill()` is never called on a dead one; the `erase` at 3040 is unconditional and `Dictionary.erase` on a missing key is a safe no-op.
- Unconditional `chosen.stop()` in the new callback (3054) is safe precisely because of the kill: `sfx()` is the ONLY writer of `sound_pool` players (grep: `sound_pool` appears at game.gd:117 and game_base.gd:250/3029/3030 and nowhere else), so a surviving tween provably still owns its slot.
- Dropping the `chosen.volume_db = -8.0` restore strands nothing audible: every play sets `chosen.volume_db = Balance.SFX_BASE_DB + vol_db` (3045) before `chosen.play()` (3047). Leaving the idle player parked at -40 dB is inert. Nothing else reads a pool player's volume.
- No re-registration race: registering a new tween under a key requires going through `sfx()`, which kills the old one first, and `tween_callback` runs synchronously inside the tween step, so a killed tween's callback cannot still fire and erase a successor's entry.
- No leak: the Dictionary is keyed by the 10 permanent pool nodes, so it is bounded at 10 entries; entries are erased on both exits (reuse at 3040, completion at 3055). Tween is RefCounted but the SceneTree holds its own ref while stepping, so erasing inside the callback is not a use-after-free.
- Multiline-lambda trap: the closing `)` on its own line (3056) is the same shape the pre-existing code used and it compiles (gate green).
- No signal is connected here, so no double-connect / CONNECT_DEFERRED exposure; no NaN path (no arithmetic on external floats); no autotest contract touched (`sound_pool`/`volume_db`/`sfx_cutoff` appear nowhere in game/scripts/autotest.gd).
- Behaviour delta beyond the defect: none audible. On the non-bug path the only change is that a stopped player is left at -40 dB instead of -8.0, overwritten on next use.
- CLAUDE.md compliance: the new `var sfx_cutoff_tweens: Dictionary = {}` sits in the BASE layer (game_base.gd:255, beside `sound_pool` at 250) per the inheritance-chain rule; the three tuning numbers moved to game/scripts/balance.gd:3435-3437 (`SFX_BASE_DB := -8.0`, `SFX_CUTOFF_DUCK_DB := -40.0`, `SFX_CUTOFF_FADE := 0.4`) per "never inline a bare tuning number"; leaving the 2.5 at boss.gd:228 alone is defensible (out-of-scope file, boss-semantic, pre-existing).

Minor, intended trade-off worth stating out loud: the reserved test consumes one of the 16 SCENERY_ACCENT_MEMBER_TRIES. An accent centre accepted just outside a large reservation (e.g. a 190px landmark clearance) can have a large share of its member rolls rejected, so a sampled group of N may render fewer than N props.
