reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SHIP IT. The defect is real, the fix is minimal and correct, the compile gate is green, and every refactored centre test is semantically identical to what it replaced.

=== 1. THE DEFECT IS REAL (confirmed against HEAD) ===
`git show HEAD:game/scripts/game_world.gd` accent member try-loop tested only lane-y, lane-x, `placed`, `group_positions` siblings and `_canopy_conflict` — no `reserved` test — then fell through to `_add_obstacle(aname, origin + apos, ...)`, which builds a `StaticBody2D` with a `CircleShape2D` collider (game/scripts/game_world.gd:3029-3038). Members are thrown up to `group_radius` (default `Balance.SCENERY_ACCENT_GROUP_RADIUS := 72.0`, balance.gd:3224) off an accepted centre, and the reservation radii are far larger than the intra-spacing the members did honour (`SCENERY_ACCENT_INTRA_SPACING := 46.0`, balance.gd:3225) — river bank `size.x/2 + 70` (game_world.gd:2454), hazard `radius + 26` (2461), notch `size.y*0.5 + 44` (2467), authored landmark `clearance` default 190.0 (2510). So a centre sitting just outside a landmark's 190px clearance could plant a collidered accent 72px deep inside it. That is exactly the 2026-08-17 "brazier sealed the corridor behind the Sable Hall" class of bug the centre test was added for.

=== 2. THE FIX ===
Helper at game/scripts/game_world.gd:2309-2314:
	func _reserved_blocks(reserved: Array, local_pos: Vector2) -> bool:
		for reservation in reserved:
			var reserve: Dictionary = reservation
			if local_pos.distance_to(reserve["pos"]) < float(reserve["radius"]):
				return true
		return false
Accent member call at game_world.gd:2881-2882, placed after the two lane `continue`s and before the `placed`/sibling/canopy tests:
	if _reserved_blocks(reserved, apos):
		continue
Correctly a `continue` inside `for member_try in Balance.SCENERY_ACCENT_MEMBER_TRIES:` (=16, balance.gd:3226), so a blocked member RE-ROLLS rather than being dropped; the pre-existing `if not member_found: continue` (2897) still drops it after 16 failures. member_idx 0 correctly skips the test — `apos = acenter`, already tested at 2851.

COORDINATE SPACE IS RIGHT, and this was the one way the fix could have been silently wrong. `reserved` is ROOM-LOCAL at every append site (2456, 2460-2461 `- origin`, 2470/2472 `- origin`, 2509 `landmark_world - origin`, 2592 `furnish_world - origin`). `acenter`/`apos` are room-local (`rng.randf_range(90.0, max_x)` at 2841, spawned as `origin + apos` at 2903). - 2694 building / 2727 landmark: the old loops only ever set `bok`/`sok` false + break; `if _reserved_blocks(...): bok = false` is equivalent because nothing downstream sets them back true (I read 2688-2701 and 2721-2739). - No §38a "cannot infer type": `var reserve: Dictionary = reservation` is an explicit annotation off a Variant loop var; `float(reserve["radius"])` is an explicit cast; `local_pos.distance_to(reserve["pos"])` passes a Variant to a typed builtin param — runtime-converted, and byte-for-byte the pattern the code it replaced already used.

- No signals touched, so no CONNECT_DEFERRED / double-connect exposure.

DEFECT CONFIRMED, and it is worse than the summary states.
The only reservation test is `game/scripts/game_world.gd:2311` — `if local_pos.distance_to(reserve["pos"]) < float(reserve["radius"]): return true`. An accepted clump CENTRE therefore clears a reservation by an arbitrarily small epsilon, not by a margin. So it is not only the 152px extreme (`SCENERY_CLUSTER_RADIUS 95.0` at `game/scripts/balance.gd:3239` x `SCENERY_HUG_STRETCH.x 1.6` at `balance.gd:3247`) that re-enters — ANY non-zero jitter can. Pre-fix, `game/scripts/game_world.gd:2791-2804` re-tested a member against lanes, `placed` spacing and the canopy rule and nothing else, and every member goes through `_add_obstacle` (`game_world.gd:2817-2819`), which always attaches a `CollisionShape2D` (`game_world.gd:3034-3039`). A tree with a collider inside the river band / hazard pool / corner bite / landmark clearance was reachable.

FRAME CORRECTNESS (the one way this fix could be silently wrong) — verified.
`reserved` is built room-local at every append: `game_world.gd:2456` (river, from `river_local` which is `rrect.position - origin`), `:2460` (`(hz["pos"] as Vector2) - origin`), `:2470`/`:2472` (`... - origin`), `:2509` (`landmark_pos = landmark_world - origin`), `:2592` (`furnish_pos = furnish_world - origin`). `mpos` is room-local — it derives from `center`, which comes from `_scatter_point(rng, pw, ph, ...)`, and is converted at the spawn: `_add_obstacle(prop, origin + mpos, ...)` (`game_world.gd:2817-2818`). So `_reserved_blocks(reserved, mpos)` at `:2803` needs no origin conversion, exactly as claimed. The centre test at `:2771` (`var ok := not _reserved_blocks(reserved, pos)`) uses the same frame. Cross-checked the sibling call sites in the same diff: the decor loop correctly converts (`:2625` `dcenter - origin`, `:2636` `dpos - origin`), the building/landmark loops pass already-local `bpos`/`spos` (`:2694`, `:2727`), accents pass local `acenter`/`apos` (`:2851`, `:2881`). No frame bug anywhere in the family.

BUG CLASSES CHECKED, ALL CLEAR.
- Variant inference: `_reserved_blocks` is explicitly `-> bool` (`game_world.gd:2309`), so `var ok := not _reserved_blocks(...)` at `:2771` infers `bool` and does not hit the CLAUDE.md "cannot infer type" trap. Inside the helper, `var reserve: Dictionary = reservation` and `float(reserve["radius"])` are both explicitly annotated. Gate confirms.
- State stranded on the early return: none. `placed.append`, `placed_n += 1` and `unique_props_seen[prop_base] = true` all sit AFTER the guard (`:2816-2822`), so a skipped member leaves nothing half-written. Skipping without incrementing `placed_n` is byte-for-byte the behaviour of the lane guards two lines above (`:2797-2800`), and the outer loop is still bounded by `guard < count * 3` (`:2745`) — no spin.
- NaN: `distance_to` on a NaN point yields NaN and `NaN < radius` is false, so a NaN prop would pass the guard — but that is the identical comparison the pre-fix inline loop used, so the fix neither adds nor removes NaN exposure.
- Signals / CONNECT_DEFERRED: this path spawns a `StaticBody2D`, connects nothing. Not applicable.
- Autotest contracts: `_test_corner_bites` (`game/scripts/autotest.gd:5302-5313`) re-runs `_spawn_scenery` and asserts no scenery body stands inside a bite; bites ARE reservations (`game_world.gd:2470-2472`), so the fix makes that assertion strictly easier to satisfy, never harder. `_test_canopy_fronts` (`autotest.gd:5239-5266`) is unaffected. Grepped for a prop-count floor — none exists; the only `obstacle_count` reference in the suite is `autotest.gd:7306`, a zone-authoring check, not a runtime tally.

reviews.title: Landmark prompt height reads the CAST SHADOW child
problems: NON-BLOCKING / commit-message accuracy: the SUMMARY names only landmark_h (2523-2526), but the same fix also rewrote the victory-gate read at game/scripts/game_world.gd:573-576 (`var gate_h := 200.0` / `_base_sprite_of(gate_node)`), which moves a visible in-game prompt by ~25px on capital_portal_story. Same defect, correct to fix, but it should be named in the commit message rather than discovered later.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SHIP IT. The defect is real, the fix is minimal and correct, it restores pre-regression behaviour rather than inventing new tuning, and the compile gate is green.

=== 1. THE DEFECT IS REAL (independently confirmed) ===
The shadow really is child 0 and really carries no hpx:

`game/scripts/game_world.gd:3447-3448`
```
		_prop_cast_shadow(body, base_spr, 12.0)
	body.add_child(base_spr)
```
`game/scripts/game_world.gd:3163-3165`
```
	cast.set_meta("cast_shadow", true)   # autotest's "one animated part" counts skip it
	body.add_child(cast)
	body.move_child(cast, 0)
```
`cast` is a hand-built Sprite2D/AnimatedSprite2D copy (game_world.gd:3122-3138) — `set_meta("cast_shadow", true)` is the ONLY meta it ever gets; `wpx`/`hpx` come from `_structure_sprite` (`game_world.gd:3270-3271`, `vis.set_meta("wpx"...)` / `vis.set_meta("hpx"...)`) and are never copied. So the old `get_child(0).get_meta("hpx", 120.0)` returned the 120.0 fallback for every structure tall enough to cast (`Balance.CAST_SHADOW_HUG_MIN_H := 14.0`, balance.gd:235 — i.e. all of them).

Git archaeology confirms it is a REGRESSION, not a design: `994a4c8` introduced `PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT`, `landmark_h` AND `gate_h` (prompts-on-the-art, owner's capital pass) and is an ancestor of `e0e9f18`, which added `body.move_child(cast, 0)` and silently broke it. `git log -S PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT -- balance.gd` shows the 0.55 constant has ONE commit (994a4c8) — it was tuned BEFORE the regression, so nothing downstream was re-tuned against the broken 120.0. The fix restores the tuned intent; it does not guess a new one.

=== 2. THE HELPER IS CORRECT ===
`game/scripts/game_world.gd:2262-2266`
```
func _base_sprite_of(body: Node2D) -> Node2D:
	for c in body.get_children():
		if (c is Sprite2D or c is AnimatedSprite2D) and c.has_meta("wpx"):
			return c as Node2D
	return null
```
- Skips the shadow (no wpx), the ground-AO disc `_add_obstacle` adds pre-sprite, CollisionShape2D, PointLight2D, and the cottage CPUParticles2D.
- First-match really is the BASE: `_add_structure` adds base_spr at :3448, then `parts` (:3452+), then colliders, then decals — all of which also carry wpx via `_structure_sprite`, but all strictly after. Same for `_add_building` (`_prop_cast_shadow` then `body.add_child(spr)`, game_world.gd:2978-2979). Godot's y-sort does not reorder children, and `_seal_portal` (game_world.gd:201-208) only iterates. No path reorders after build.
- The `has_meta("cast_shadow")` skip idiom already exists elsewhere (`_seal_portal` :202; autotest.gd:4861/4877/4961) — this is consistent with house practice, not a novel guard.

=== 3. `_front_of` REWRITE IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING ===
Old `_front_of` already looped for the wpx child (it never used get_child(0)), so it was never buggy. New version (`game_world.gd:2271-2283`) is a pure refactor: same first-match, same `position + Vector2(get("offset")) * scale` fold-in, same zero-rect fallback when nothing matches. The autotest canopy contract that calls it (`game/scripts/autotest.gd:5247-5249`, `var f: Dictionary = game._front_of(body, body.position)` gated on `(f["rect"] as Rect2).size.x > 0.0`) is unaffected.

=== 4. GDSCRIPT / CODING_GUIDELINES §38 TRAPS — CLEAN ===
- No `:=` on a Variant expression. `var landmark_h := 120.0` / `var gate_h := 200.0` infer float from literals; the Variant `get_meta` result is wrapped in the `float()` builtin before assignment, and `var cp: Vector2 = ...` stays explicitly annotated. `var front_spr := _base_sprite_of(body)` infers from the declared `-> Node2D`.
- No new signal connections → no double-connect, no CONNECT_DEFERRED/physics-flush exposure.
- No NaN path: hpx = `native.y * (target_w / maxf(1.0, native.x))`, always finite.
- No state stranded on an early return — the two new guards fall back to exactly the constants the buggy read produced, so the failure mode is the old behaviour, not a half-initialised node.
- No `class_name` added → no `--import` requirement.
- Compile gate green in the worktree: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, RC=0.

=== 5. BEHAVIOUR DELTA — MEASURED, BOUNDED, ALL IN THE INTENDED DIRECTION ===
I parsed `Terrains.STRUCTURES` + the PNG headers and cross-referenced every authored landmark that actually has a `"uses"` entry (the only place `landmark_h` is consumed, `game_world.gd:2581`). All 13 are tall, so every prompt moves UP, none down:
  capital_portal_depths 202.8px (+45.6), portal_crucible 233.1 (+62.2), portal_story 246.0 (+69.3), market_stall 252.9 (+73.1), grand_archive 265.9 (+80.3), wildfang_fangmoot 269.4 (+82.2), accord_longhouse 286.5 (+91.6), rot_chapel 314.3 (+106.9), crown_fountain 350.7 (+126.9), sable_hall 366.4 (+135.5), crown_spire_gate 369.7 (+137.3), emberward_gate 380.1 (+143.0), alembic_station 222.2 (+56.2).
  Victory gate (`game_world.gd:573-576`, capital_portal_story, 521x566 source @ w=226.48): gate_h 200.0 -> 246.0, label -144 -> -169.3.
That is the label landing at 55% up the art, which is literally what the constant is named for. No structure with a `uses` station is short enough to make the prompt drop.

=== 6. NOT REVIEWED ===
`git diff -- game/scripts/game_world.gd` also carries two unrelated sibling fixes I did NOT review per the one-fix scope: `_canopy_tree` (game_world.gd:2201-2202, tree_stump excluded from canopy handling) and `_reserved_blocks` (game_world.gd:2303-2312, clump/group members re-tested against reservations). They compile; their correctness is someone else's review.

Changed nothing. Ran only the compile gate.

reviews.title: Victory-gate prompt height reads the CAST SHADOW child
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: sound — I would ship this hunk.

## 1. The defect is real, and I confirmed every link in the chain

`game/scripts/game_world.gd:571` builds the gate as a structure:
```
var gate_node := _add_structure("capital_portal_story", gate_world)
```

- `game/scripts/terrains.gd:1227` — the def is `{"sprite": "capital_portal_story", "w": 226.4844, "colliders": [...]}`. No `"cast": false`, so `game/scripts/game_world.gd:3446` (`if def.get("cast", true):`) fires `_prop_cast_shadow(body, base_spr, 12.0)` BEFORE `body.add_child(base_spr)` at :3448.
- `game/scripts/game_world.gd:3164-3165` — `body.add_child(cast)` then `body.move_child(cast, 0)`. The shadow is child 0 unconditionally.
- The shadow copy is a fresh `Sprite2D`/`AnimatedSprite2D` that only ever gets `cast.set_meta("cast_shadow", true)` (:3163) — it carries no `wpx`/`hpx`. So the old `gate_node.get_child(0).get_meta("hpx", 200.0)` returned the 200.0 fallback every single time. Defect confirmed, not hypothetical.
- Neither early-out in `_prop_cast_shadow` applies: `Balance.CAST_SHADOW_A := 0.30` (`balance.gd:226`, > 0) and the rendered height clears `CAST_SHADOW_HUG_MIN_H := 14.0` (`balance.gd:235`).

The claimed ~246 px checks out numerically. `game/assets/sprites/capital_portal_story.png` is 521x566; `_structure_sprite` (`game_world.gd:3263-3271`) sets `hpx = native.y * (target_w / native.x)` = 566 x 226.4844/521 = **246.05**. So the prompt was sitting 25.3 px too low (`-(34 + 200*0.55)` = -144 vs `-(34 + 246.05*0.55)` = -169.3, `PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT := 0.55`, `balance.gd:610`). That is the whole behaviour change — nothing else moves.

Extra corroboration that this exact structure has an animated base + a shadow child: `game/scripts/autotest.gd:4940` lists `capital_portal_story` in `capital_fire_structures` and the comment at `game_world.gd:3163` says the shadow is exactly what that test's "one animated part" count skips.

## 2. The helper is correct for this call site

`game/scripts/game_world.gd:2262-2266`:
```
func _base_sprite_of(body: Node2D) -> Node2D:
	for c in body.get_children():
		if (c is Sprite2D or c is AnimatedSprite2D) and c.has_meta("wpx"):
			return c as Node2D
	return null
```
- The `has_meta("wpx")` filter is the load-bearing part: it is what rejects the shadow (which passes the type test, since the shadow of an AnimatedSprite2D base is itself an AnimatedSprite2D).
- Child order inside `_add_structure` guarantees the BASE wins over the other wpx-carrying children. `_structure_sprite` also stamps `wpx` on composite `parts` (:3466) and `decals` (:3509), but both are added strictly after `body.add_child(base_spr)` (:3448), and the only `move_child` in the whole builder is the shadow's to index 0. `capital_portal_story` has neither parts nor decals anyway. `_floor_glow` uses a plain `parent.add_child(g)` (:4757) — no reordering.
- `_prop_visual` (:3227-3233) returns either `Art.anim_prop(name)` (an `AnimatedSprite2D`, `art.gd:3220`) or a `Sprite2D`, so the type filter can never miss a real base. For this gate the base is the AnimatedSprite2D (autotest asserts the 4-frame integrated fire strip), which the filter accepts.

## 3. Adversarial checks — all clean

- **Variant inference (the CLAUDE.md trap):** none. `var gate_h := 200.0` infers float from a float literal; `var gate_base := _base_sprite_of(gate_node)` infers from the explicit `-> Node2D` return type, not from a Variant expression. The Variant that *is* present (`get_meta`) is wrapped: `float(gate_base.get_meta("hpx", 200.0))` (:576). Compile gate agrees.
- **NaN path:** `hpx = native.y * (target_w / maxf(1.0, native.x))` — the divisor is floored at 1.0, both operands finite. No NaN can reach the Label y.
- **Null path / stranded state:** the `if gate_base != null` guard is defensive only (unreachable for a structure), and on the null branch `gate_h` keeps the exact pre-fix value of 200.0 — a strict no-op fallback, no half-initialized state, no early return skipping the hotspot wiring.
- **Signals:** nothing connected or disconnected here; no CONNECT_DEFERRED concern (no physics-signal spawn added).
- **Autotest contract:** nothing asserts the gate prompt height. `game/scripts/tests/test_ch1.gd:559` only checks `game.victory_gates_up`; `PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT` appears in no test. `autotest.gd:4940`'s structure test counts children by type/meta and is unaffected by a read-only helper.
- **Type coercion of `gate_node`:** `_add_structure` returns `StaticBody2D`, which is a `Node2D` — the parameter type is satisfied.
- **Behaviour beyond the defect:** none. The only observable delta is the Label y on the three victory gates.

## 4. CLAUDE.md compliance

- No inlined tuning number introduced — `200.0` is a pre-existing structural fallback, not a new knob, and the real value now comes from art meta. `PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT` still comes from `balance.gd`.
- Correct layer: gate spawning is `game_world` (graph/rooms/spawning/gates) per the inheritance chain; `_base_sprite_of` is a `game_world`-local helper used only by `game_world` callers, so no derived→base violation.
- The fix now matches the landmark idiom verbatim (`game_world.gd:2581`: `child.position.y = -(use_dy + landmark_h * Balance.PROP_PROMPT_HEIGHT)`), which is the convention this call site was clearly meant to follow.
- No mobile edit (correct — `game/` is source of truth; `mobile/` re-sync is a separate ritual and this branch has not run it for this change; worth remembering before staging).

## 5. Scope note (not a defect in this hunk)

`git diff -- game/scripts/game_world.gd` is much larger than this fix: it also carries the `_canopy_tree()` tree_stump exclusion, the `_front_of` refactor onto the same helper (finding 4, which is what makes this hunk a pure reuse), and the `_reserved_blocks()` extraction plus four new clump/group-member reservation re-tests. I did not review those — they are separate findings. My verdict covers only lines 573-576 and the `_base_sprite_of` helper they depend on.

## 6. Two cosmetic remarks, neither blocking

- The `200.0` default inside `get_meta("hpx", 200.0)` (:576) is now redundant with the initializer on :573. Harmless duplication; the landmark twin at :2523-2526 has the same shape, so it is at least consistent.
- The one thing a number cannot settle: whether the prompt reading 25 px higher looks right on the arch in-game. Per CLAUDE.md that is the owner's call, not a gate's.

reviews.title: `tree_stump` classed as a TREE by the `contains("tree")` heuristic
problems: autotest.gd:5251 still classifies audited props with the raw `.contains("tree")` substring while the engine no longer does, and decor-path stumps reach that audit (game_world.gd:2651) through a path that has no canopy check at all. The fix's 16 px northward art shift (game_world.gd:3058) re-rolls that seed-dependent assertion: a stump landing north of a building whose art it overlaps would fail _test_canopy_fronts with a message about a defect that, after this change, is by design not a defect. Close it by calling game._canopy_tree(...) there — the audit already calls game._structure_is_tree at autotest.gd:5247.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: ship it. The defect is real, the fix is minimal and correct, compile gate green (COMPILE OK, 121 scripts). One follow-up worth doing (autotest predicate divergence), not a blocker.

EVIDENCE THE DEFECT WAS REAL
- terrains.gd:75-80 `const SOLID_DECOR := { "mushroom": true, "toadstool": true, "tree_stump": true, "signpost": true, }` — tree_stump is the ONLY key containing "tree", so the claim "nothing else changes" holds.
- balance.gd:3291 `"tree_stump": 42.0,` (SCENERY_RENDER_WIDTH) + game_world.gd:3044-3049 `if not is_tree:` / `# The fixed 3x2 ellipse was tuned for 64px+ props; the solid-decor / # smalls (toadstool 39, stump 42) shrink it to their footprint.` — the shrink literally names the stump and the substring test was skipping it. Confirmed.
- Collider genuinely untouched: game_world.gd:3036-3037 `shape.radius = float(Balance.SCENERY_COLLIDER_RADIUS.get(family_base, 13.0 if is_tree else 11.0))` and balance.gd:3313 `... "tree_stump": 13.0,` — explicit entry wins, the is_tree default never applied.

GODOT 4.4 CORRECTNESS
- game_world.gd:2203-2204 `func _canopy_tree(base: String) -> bool:` / `return base.contains("tree") and not Terrains.SOLID_DECOR.has(base)`. Dictionary.has() is typed bool, so `var is_tree := _canopy_tree(...)` (game_world.gd:2247, :3028) infers cleanly — no Variant-inference trap. No signals, no early-return stranded state, no NaN path, no new class_name (no --import needed). Compile gate run: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0.

NO HIDDEN CALL SITES / SCOPE IS TIGHT
- _prop_art_rect has exactly 4 callers (game_world.gd:2779, 2812, 2860, 2893), all already gated by _canopy_tree, so the bottom 38->22 change is unreachable for stumps: consistent, not behaviour-bearing.
- _wind_scenery has 2 callers (game_world.gd:2668 decor-sticker path, :3064 obstacle path). A stump never reaches :2668 because the SOLID_DECOR branch at :2644-2653 calls _add_obstacle and `continue`s first. Only :3064 changes.
- deadtree* and the seven tree_* variant families (terrains.gd:32-39) are unaffected — none in SOLID_DECOR. tree_stump is in no PROP_VARIANT_GROUPS family, so prop_base("tree_stump") == "tree_stump" and the SOLID_DECOR lookup (keyed by base) hits.
- tree_stump appears ONLY in "decor" arrays (terrains.gd:133, story.gd:782, content/ch2_hub.gd:26), never in obstacles/accents — so the three canopy gates it now bypasses (:2778, :2811, :2858) never saw it. No placement change in practice.

REAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (intended, but owner-visible)
- game_world.gd:3050 `shadow.position = Vector2(0, 38 if is_tree else 22)` and :3058 `var base_y := 38.0 if is_tree else 22.0` mean the stump SPRITE moves 16 px north relative to its body, on top of the shadow change (4x2.4 @38 -> 3x2*0.656 @22) and the loss of the wind material. The shift aligns the art bottom with the collider (cs.position = Vector2(0,10), r=13 -> bottom +23), which is the correct read, but every existing room's stumps move on screen. Worth naming to the owner rather than filing as "shadow only".

FOLLOW-UP (should-fix, not a blocker)
- autotest.gd:5251 still uses the raw substring: `elif body.has_meta("prop") and Terrains.prop_base(String(body.get_meta("prop"))).contains("tree"):`, building each tree rect from the RENDERED sprite (autotest.gd:5255-5260, `centre := body.position + c.position`). Decor-path stumps DO reach that audit — game_world.gd:2651 `zone_scenery[zi].append(_add_obstacle(decor_name, dpos, ...))` — and the decor path runs no canopy check at all. So the engine now says "a stump has no crown" while _test_canopy_fronts still says it does, and this edit shifts every stump's audited rect 16 px north, re-rolling a seed-dependent assertion. Slightly stronger than the summary's "pre-existing, unchanged".
- Mitigating: it fails LOUD and early (autotest.gd:1027 is in the core-systems tier that --quick covers), and the audit already calls a game_world predicate one line up (autotest.gd:5247 `game._structure_is_tree(...)`), so the close is a one-token change to `game._canopy_tree(...)` with established precedent.

NITS (no action)
- The predicate encodes "SOLID_DECOR is never a canopy": a future leafy SOLID_DECOR entry would silently lose wind. It keys on the base, so a variant name of a solid-decor family would slip through — unreachable today (no stump variant group).
- mobile/game/scripts/game_world.gd:2202 still carries the old substring. Correct per the desktop-source-of-truth policy, but the branch owes `sync_mobile --apply --gate` before staging.

reviews.title: _apply_hazards re-fetches the "enemies" group inside the per-hazard loop — O(hazards x enemies) every 0.4 s
problems: NON-BLOCKING, accuracy of the claim: the FIX CLAIMED line says the defect is 'O(hazards x enemies) every 0.4 s', but the fix does not change that complexity. game_flow.gd:2247-2250 still walks every mob for every physical hazard; what was removed is the per-hazard Array allocation and the per-enemy Dictionary lookups (the constant factor). The summary body is honest about this ('removes the allocation storm and most of the constant factor'), so this is a headline-vs-body mismatch, not a code problem. If the owner expected the O() to change, only the skipped active_rooms/spatial gate would have done it.

NON-BLOCKING, tiny cost regression on a cold path: hoisting the three reads to game_flow.gd:2224-2226 makes them unconditional. Previously h["pos"] and h["radius"] were only touched inside the player-in-range condition or the physical-hazard inner loop, so a dedicated server (lp == null) with a non-physical patch ('heal', 'poison', 'churned') now does 2 dict lookups per hazard it used to skip. Utterly dwarfed by the win; noted only for completeness.

NON-BLOCKING, pre-existing NaN hole the patch touched and left: game_flow.gd:2250 `e.global_position.distance_to(hpos) > hrad` — a NaN enemy position yields NaN, `NaN > hrad` is false, so the guard does NOT skip and the hazard applies to a NaN actor. Compare game_flow.gd:2279 twelve lines below, which does guard the river pass with `e.global_position.is_finite()`. This is the known NaN soft-lock family; the diff neither introduces nor fixes it, but this line was in the edit's blast radius and adding `and e.global_position.is_finite()` would have been free.

NON-BLOCKING style nit: `var mobs: Array = get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")` (game_flow.gd:2200) explicitly WIDENS the engine's `Array[Node]` return to untyped `Array`, which is what demotes the two loop vars to Variant. `var mobs := get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")` would infer `Array[Node]` and keep `node` typed. Purely cosmetic — the `as Enemy` cast makes both forms compile and behave identically.

BRANCH-LEVEL, not this fix's defect: mobile/game/scripts/game_flow.gd is still the old code (`func _apply_hazards` at mobile line 2186, no const, no hoist), so the mobile mirror has drifted per the CLAUDE.md sync policy. The whole branch has 20 modified files under game/ and zero under mobile/, so this is a pre-commit `python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate` step for the branch, not something this diff should have carried.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: SHIP IT. The diff is correct, compiles, and every safety claim in the summary checks out against the code. Compile gate run in the worktree: `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`, exit 0.

WHAT THE DIFF ACTUALLY IS (game/scripts/game_flow.gd, one file, three hunks, nothing else touched):
- game_flow.gd:2186 `const HAZARD_PHYSICAL := ["ice", "slow", "lava"]`
- game_flow.gd:2200 `var mobs: Array = get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")`, reused by both the reset loop (2201) and the inner enemy pass (2248)
- game_flow.gd:2224-2226 `var htype: String = h["type"]` / `var hpos: Vector2 = h["pos"]` / `var hrad: float = h["radius"]`

DOES IT FIX THE DEFECT? Yes, the part it claims to. The per-hazard `get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")` is gone; one fetch per tick. Caveat below (P1): the O(hazards x enemies) *iteration* is untouched, only the allocation + dict lookups are.

CORRECTNESS — each risk checked, all clear:

1. Stale-snapshot / dangling reference (the real hazard of a group hoist). Enemies can only LEAVE the group inside this loop, never join it: the only `add_to_group("enemies")` in the repo is enemy.gd:343, in the constructor path, and nothing in `take_damage` -> `die()` builds an Enemy. Both removal sites set the flag first — enemy.gd:1515 `dying = true` ... enemy.gd:1525 `remove_from_group("enemies")`, and enemy.gd:2542 `dying = true` ... enemy.gd:2553 `remove_from_group("enemies")` — so the pre-existing guard at game_flow.gd:2250 `if e == null or e.dying or ...: continue` reproduces the old fetch's filtering exactly. No node is freed synchronously: `_death_fade` (enemy.gd:1309-1313) tweens then `tween_callback(queue_free)`, and the only other free is enemy.gd:1517 `queue_free()` on a not-in-tree mob (which was never in the fetch). There is no `.free()` anywhere in enemy.gd. So the held references stay valid for the whole tick. Claim verified.

2. Nothing re-enters or mutates `hazards` synchronously from the damage call. `e.take_damage(5.0, Vector2.ZERO, false, true)` passes `silent = true`, which gates off REFLECT (enemy.gd:2446) and COUNTER (enemy.gd:2451). `die()`'s hazard-spawning trait uses `_hazard.call_deferred(...)` (enemy.gd:2564) and its loot/XP hook is `game.on_enemy_died.call_deferred(self)` (enemy.gd:2592). `wake_pack` (game_world.gd:1475-1483) only sets flags.

3. Type-safety of the three new typed locals: there is exactly ONE construction site for a hazards entry, game_world.gd:4806, reached only through `func _add_hazard(zi: int, type: String, pos: Vector2, radius: float, ...)` at game_world.gd:4768 — and the co-op path funnels through the same function (net_session.gd:1806). So `String` / `Vector2` / `float` are guaranteed; no new crash surface. (boss.gd:1834 only adds a `no_melt` key.)

4. Ordering: `hpos` is read at game_flow.gd:2225, AFTER the drift block at 2213-2221 mutates `h["pos"]`. A drifting spore cloud therefore reads its moved position, same as before. Getting this backwards would have been a silent one-tick-stale bug; the patch got it right and says why in the comment.

5. §38a Variant inference: `var e := node as Enemy` at game_flow.gd:2249 now iterates an untyped `Array`, so `node` is Variant — but `as T` carries the static type T, so inference holds. The identical pattern already exists in the same function at game_flow.gd:2296 (`var ds := scenery[i] as Sprite2D` over an untyped Array). Compile gate confirms.

6. `const` in the middle of the file is legal GDScript and matches this file's own convention (game_flow.gd:679, 683, 1468, 1469). No name collision: `HAZARD_PHYSICAL` appears nowhere else in the repo, and none of game_base.gd / game_world.gd / game.gd declare it. In Godot 4 a const Array is read-only at runtime, so nothing can mutate the shared list.

7. No new bug in the classes you named: no signals touched (no double-connect, no CONNECT_DEFERRED question), no early return added so no state stranded, `lp.hazard_speed`/`e.hazard_speed` resets unchanged, no NaN path introduced, no autotest contract broken (nothing in autotest.gd references `_apply_hazards` or `HAZARD_PHYSICAL`; the terrain/hazard sections at autotest.gd:2317-2340 and 4345-4361 exercise it through the normal 2.5Hz tick and are unaffected).

8. CLAUDE.md: HAZARD_PHYSICAL is a membership list, not a tuning knob — correctly kept out of balance.gd per §38f. Comment idiom matches. No codex/BOSS_KINDS/shot-rig surface.

9. The skipped `active_rooms` gate was the right call and the stated reason is verified: enemy.gd:825 `if zone_idx >= 0 and not game.active_rooms.has(zone_idx): return` sits inside `_physics_process` only, so a frozen offscreen mob genuinely still eats `take_damage` from this function every 0.4s. Gating here would be a gameplay change, not an optimization. Correctly deferred to the owner.

Minor bonus: using one snapshot for both the reset loop and the inner passes is slightly MORE consistent than before, where each fetch could see a different set.

reviews.title: Moot never starts a new shop turn: no income, no tray refresh after turn 1
problems: Scope creep (benign, worth naming in the commit): the `turn` half of the snap fixes a SECOND, pre-existing bug. Before this change `_fight_view`'s topbar already printed the post-increment turn and, via `_persona(mo)`, the NEXT caller's portrait while replaying the fight you just fought (`fangmoot.gd:369` label, `378` portrait). Only the `fangs` half was forced by the income fix. It is a correct improvement, but it is a behaviour change beyond the stated defect.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: ship it. The defect is real, the fix is minimal and correct, and the compile gate is green (`COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`).

DEFECT CONFIRMED
`begin_turn()` is the only income+tray refresh (`game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_moot.gd:87-89`):
  func begin_turn() -> void:
      fangs = income()
      _roll_tray(true)
A repo-wide grep for `begin_turn` returns exactly five call sites: the definition, the bot's warband builder (`fangmoot_bot.gd:43`), autotest (`autotest.gd:9942`), the selftest (`fangmoot_selftest.gd:185`), and `fangmoot.gd`'s `_start`. None in the UI's per-turn path. So the human player got 10 fangs ONCE for a 15-turn moot (`balance.gd:3006 FANGMOOT_MAX_TURNS := 15`) and a tray frozen at turn-1 contents, while the AI opponent was built through the correct cadence (`fangmoot_bot.gd:41-44`: `for t in ... : m.begin_turn(); take_turn(...); m.advance_no_fight()`). Confirmed.

FIX IS CORRECT
`game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd:797-798` — `if not mo.done: mo.begin_turn()` after `mo.call_moot(...)` (line 792). Three things check out:
- Placement AFTER call_moot is required, not cosmetic: `call_moot` does `turn += 1` at `fangmoot_moot.gd:409`, and the tray size/tier gates read `turn` (`_tray_tokens` 117-122, `_tray_supply` 124-125, `_named_slot` 127-132, `_available_tiers` 134-139). Calling before would refill the tray at the turn just fought.
- The `not mo.done` guard matches where `done` is set (`fangmoot_moot.gd:410-418`, win/loss/timeout). Continue then routes through `open()` → `_result` (`fangmoot.gd:72-73`), which never reads fangs/tray, so a refreshed purse would be dead-but-wrong state. Correct guard.
- Cadence matches the canonical loop exactly one begin_turn per turn: `_start` (line 697) seeds turn 1, `_call` seeds every turn after. No double-grant: `fangs` is only ever written by `begin_turn`, `roll` (-1), `buy_*` (-cost), `sell` (+level), `from_dict`.

NO NEW BUG FOUND
- No Variant-inference trap: `var snap := {"turn": ..., "fangs": ...}` is a Dictionary literal, and both reads wrap the Variant — `var shown_turn := int(snap.get("turn", mo.turn))` (line 349). The ternary `var t := mo.turn if at_turn < 0 else at_turn` (line 813) infers int from two typed ints. Compile gate proves it.
- No signal work touched; `arena.finished.connect(...)` (line 850) is still on a fresh arena per `_fight_view`, so no double-connect.
- No state stranded: the only early return (`fangmoot.gd:786-787`) precedes every mutation.
- No autotest contract broken — autotest §4 (`autotest.gd:9938-9943`) and `fangmoot_selftest.gd:180-186` drive `FangmootMoot` directly and never enter `_call`. `shot_fangmoot.gd:31` calls `_call` but only screenshots.
- No inlined tuning number: income comes from `fangmoot_moot.gd:52-53` → `Balance.FANGMOOT_FANGS`. The no-carry-over behaviour matches `balance.gd:2997` (`# shop income per turn (flat; no carry-over)`) and PROPOSALS/FANGMOOT.md §5 ("No interest, no carry-over").
- Frozen cards survive correctly: `begin_turn` passes `keep_frozen=true` (`fangmoot_moot.gd:89`), and `_roll_tray` retains them (91-97) — matches the design line "a frozen tray card survives the roll and the turn".
- The `snap` plumbing is required, not decorative: without it the fight bar would print the refilled 10 fangs over a fight bought with 2. Defaults are safe — `_full_topbar(..., snap := {})` with empty snap reproduces the old `mo.turn`/`mo.fangs` reads exactly, and the shop's call at line 305 passes nothing.

I would ship this.

reviews.title: Board drop-zones index by board slot while the arena renders compacted
problems: Behaviour change beyond the strict defect (acceptable, and the better of the two options): an EMPTY slot's drop-zone now sits at a trailing pedestal rather than its board-index pedestal, so dropping a card on the visibly-blank pedestal can insert it at a board index ahead of an existing token (board [A, null, B]: the blank pedestal is the 3rd, the buy lands at board index 1 and re-renders between A and B). Self-consistent after the re-render at fangmoot.gd:768 `open(m)`, but worth one line in the branch notes so it is not later mistaken for a new defect.

Mobile mirror not updated: mobile/game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd:430 still reads `var lp: Vector2 = arena._slot_pos(0, i)`. Branch-level rather than this fix's obligation (all 20 modified files on the branch are under game/), but the CLAUDE.md re-sync ritual (`python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate`) is owed before staging.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: ship it. The defect is real, the fix is minimal, correct GDScript, and I found no new bug.

1) DEFECT CONFIRMED (verified independently, not by trusting the summary)
- Renderer compacts. game/scripts/ui/fangmoot_arena.gd:151-159 `func _lay_side(band: Array, side: int, uid: int) -> int:` / `var idx := 0` / `for spec in band:` / `if spec == null: continue` / `_make_token(spec, side, idx, uid)` / `idx += 1` — a null does NOT consume a pedestal.
- The band handed in preserves holes: fangmoot_moot.gd:367-373 `func fight_band() -> Array:` ... `if s == null:` / `band.append(null)` / `continue`. The shop mounts exactly that at fangmoot.gd:304 `arena.set_bands(mo.fight_band(), m.fm_opp)`, and the overlay is built over that same arena at fangmoot.gd:307 `_board_overlay(m, root, mo, arena)`.
- Holes are reachable in normal play: fangmoot_moot.gd:267 `board[slot_idx] = null` (sell), :281 `board[from_idx] = null` (bond branch of move), :283 `board[from_idx] = dest` (swap with an empty dest moves the hole), and buy_token places at any empty index (:211-221).
- Old code used the raw board index (`arena._slot_pos(0, i)`), so with board [A, null, B] the zone addressing B sat over the wrong pedestal and the pedestal showing B carried the zone for empty slot 1: dragging A onto the visible B ran `move(0,1)` instead of the swap the player saw. Real and user-visible.

2) THE FIX IS CORRECT
- fangmoot.gd:443-456 `_render_order` mirrors `_lay_side` exactly: filled slots take 0..f-1 in board order, empty slots take f..n-1 — precisely the `idx` value `_make_token` receives for the token in board slot i.
- It is a bijection over 0..n-1 (first loop consumes 0..f-1, second f..n-1), so no two zones can land on the same pedestal; no zone can steal another's drops, and the old identity-permutation non-overlap property is preserved.
- Only the render position is remapped; gameplay indices are untouched: fangmoot.gd:461 `var slot = mo.board[i]`, :475 `return {"fm": "board", "idx": i}`, :761 `mo.move(int(data.get("idx", 0)), i)`, :765-767 `mo.buy_token(idx, i)` / `buy_charm` / `buy_brew`.
- `_slot_drop` ends with `open(m)` (fangmoot.gd:768), so the overlay is rebuilt after every mutation — the order array cannot go stale against its board.

3) GODOT 4.4 GDSCRIPT — clean
- `var order := _render_order(mo)` infers fine because `_render_order` has an explicit `-> PackedInt32Array` return type; not the Variant-inference trap in CLAUDE.md / CODING_GUIDELINES §38.
- `out.resize(...)` discards an int return; RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED is off by default and game/project.godot has no `debug/gdscript` warnings block at all.
- `arena._slot_pos(0, order[i])` passes a typed int; `var lp: Vector2 =` is annotated. No NaN path (integer index maths only), no signal connected here (no double-connect / CONNECT_DEFERRED concern), no early return so no stranded state.

4) COMPILE GATE: `tools\Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win64_console.exe --headless --path game --script res://check_compile.gd` → `COMPILE OK (121 scripts)`. Changed nothing in the worktree.

5) AUTOTEST CONTRACT: unaffected. `_test_fangmoot` (autotest.gd:9885+) exercises FangmootSim/Moot/Bot/Codes only; nothing outside the two UI files references `_board_overlay`, `_render_order`, `_slot_pos` or `_lay_side`.

6) CLAUDE.md compliance: no bare tuning number introduced; the edit stayed in the one scoped file; the stale comment claiming the zones "can never drift" was corrected rather than left lying. Choosing the UI-side remap over adding `_compact()` to fangmoot_moot.gd is the right call — compacting the board would silently reorder the fight line on every sell, a genuine gameplay change (slot 0 is the sim's front-liner, per the comment at fangmoot_arena.gd:161-164).

Two non-blocking observations are in `problems`; neither changes the verdict.

reviews.title: Fight screen names the NEXT turn's caller over the fight you are watching
problems: Non-blocking, acknowledged: fangmoot.gd:371-372 still pass mo.crests / mo.scars, so the CRESTS/SCARS pips show the post-fight tally during the replay and spoil the banner _arena_done reveals. Same root cause, outside the stated finding; _arena_done (:857) does not rebuild the bar, so blanking them would remove the only pip feedback on that screen. Non-blocking, PRE-EXISTING and untouched but on the same top bar: _cycle_speed (fangmoot.gd:426-427) only assigns m.fm_speed and never rebuilds the view, while fangmoot_arena.gd:363 "\t_speed = maxf(0.5, speed)" captures the value at play(). reviews.title: Conceding on turn 1 leaks the opponent warband into the next moot, across tables
problems: NON-BLOCKING (latent fragility, not a defect in this diff): the root cause -- a cache key with no moot identity (fangmoot.gd:336) -- is still there; the fix works only because _start is currently the sole constructor of m.fm_moot. Any future path that builds a moot without going through _start reintroduces the leak silently. Keying _ensure_opp on the moot's seed as well as its turn would be immune, but that is a larger edit than the task asked for and I would not hold the fix for it.

NON-BLOCKING (staging obligation, branch-wide not fix-specific): mobile/game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd already differs from HEAD's game/ copy and does not carry this change, so the CLAUDE.md re-sync (python tools/sync_mobile.py --apply --gate) is still owed before this branch is staged.
reviews.notes:
VERDICT: sound — I would ship it. The 4-line edit is exactly the claimed fix, nothing more, and I could not construct a case where it strands state or changes unrelated behaviour.

THE DEFECT IS REAL (reproduced by reading, not assumed):
- Cache guard, `game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd:336`: `if m.fm_opp_turn != mo.turn or m.fm_opp.is_empty():` — no moot/table/seed in the key.
- The `is_empty()` half is genuinely dead as a guard: `FangmootBot.build_warband` returns `m.fight_band()` (`game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_bot.gd:46`), and `fight_band()` appends `null` for every empty slot (`game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_moot.gd:367-374`), so the array is always FANGMOOT_BOARD entries long. Confirmed the summary's claim.
- Every moot starts at turn 1: `game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_moot.gd:17` `var turn := 1`.
- HEAD's only reset was in `_call` (`git show HEAD:game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd`, `m.fm_opp_turn = -1` right after `mo.call_moot(...)`). `_concede` (now lines 778-782) sets `scars/done/outcome` and never touches the cache. So: shop turn 1 → `_moot` → `_ensure_opp` sets `fm_opp_turn = 1` → Concede → `_result` → new moot at turn 1 → guard sees `1 == 1` and non-empty → the previous table's caller warband is previewed AND fought. Concede-on-turn-1 is the only leaking path (any later turn leaves `fm_opp_turn != 1`, and any fought turn leaves it at -1), which matches the summary exactly.

THE FIX CLOSES IT, AND THE PLACEMENT IS THE UNIVERSAL GATE:
- `game/scripts/ui/fangmoot.gd:691-696` — `m.fm_opp = []` / `m.fm_opp_turn = -1` immediately after `FangmootMoot.new(...)`; `-1` can never equal a moot turn, so `_ensure_opp` rebuilds against the new moot's persona/table/seed.
- `_start` really is the only constructor of the session moot: `grep FangmootMoot.new` over `game/` hits only `fangmoot.gd:691` plus the bot/bench/selftest/autotest harnesses, which build their own throwaway moots and never touch `m.fm_opp`. Both result-screen buttons route through it or through `_start` afterwards — "Play again" (`fangmoot.gd:900-903`: `m.fm_moot = null; _start(m, t)`) and "Back to the Circle" (`:904-906`: `m.fm_moot = null; open(m)` → `_hub`, and the hub's only entry is `_start.bind(m, ...)` at `:290`). The shot rig also enters via `UIFangmoot._start` (`game/shot_fangmoot.gd:20`). `fm_moot` is session-lived and never restored from a save (`game/scripts/menus.gd:17`), so there is no deserialize path that bypasses the gate.
- Agreed that a duplicate reset in `_concede` would be dead: between concede and the next `_start`, only `_result` and `_hub` render, and neither reads `fm_opp` (its only readers are `:304` and `:336-338`).

NO NEW BUG FOUND:
- GDScript/Godot 4.4: plain assignments to declared members (`game/scripts/menus.gd:20-21` `var fm_opp: Array = []`, `var fm_opp_turn := -1`) — no `:=` inference on a Variant (§38a), no signal work, no early return to strand state, no NaN path, no physics-flush spawn.
- Reassignment rather than `.clear()` is the correct form here and matters: `call_moot` aliases the same array into the moot (`game/scripts/fangmoot/fangmoot_moot.gd:398` `last_opp = opp_band`), which `_fight_view` replays via `arena.set_bands(mo.last_band, mo.last_opp)`. A `.clear()` in `_start` would have emptied a still-referenced band; `= []` cannot. Also lines up with §38g's "never `.clear()`".
- Autotest contract untouched: `_test_fangmoot` (`game/scripts/autotest.gd:9885-9988`) exercises sim/moot/bot/codes/data/seam only — it never calls into `UIFangmoot`.
- Behaviour delta is exactly the defect: on a first moot the fields are already `[]`/-1, and after any fought moot `_call` already left `fm_opp_turn = -1`, so only the concede-on-turn-1 case changes.
- Comment style is fine under §38i (a why-comment, no §-number reference).

I checked only that they do not conflict with this one — they don't: `_call` still clears `fm_opp_turn` at `:793` before `begin_turn`, so the next shop turn rebuilds normally.
